# Controls and their settings

<!-- Generated by ErikwnkWFUI.Tests (ControlTableGenerator). Do not edit: run tools/Update-ControlTable.ps1. -->

What every control and window of the library has of its own: properties (the default is that of a new control in the dark theme with the blue
accent; `-` where it depends on the screen or is not a plain value), events and methods, and the `UIStyles` factory methods that make it. A control keeps
everything else of its standard WinForms base class; the properties it **ignores** (draws its own way) are listed per control. A type without a
constructor that takes no parameters shows the defaults of its standard factory called with its default arguments. After the controls come the other
public types (helpers, static entry points, enumerations) and at the end the factory classes.

## CardPanel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.CardPanel` - based on `Panel`

A card: a panel with smoothly rounded corners and a thin line around it, for a group of controls on a page (`UIStyles.Panels.CreateCardStandard`). It paints what is behind it in its corners, so it works on any page color.

Made by `UIStyles.Panels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the thin line around the card; follows the theme (and, on a color, is moved until it is seen against it) until it is set, `Empty` gives that back. |
| `BorderStyle` | `BorderStyle` | `FixedSingle` | get, set | Whether the thin line around the card is drawn: `FixedSingle` (the default; `Fixed3D` looks the same) or `None`. It hides the `BorderStyle` of the standard panel, which would have the system draw a rectangular frame over the rounded corners (the panel's own is always none; do not set it through a `Panel` variable). |
| `CornerRadius` | `int` | `8` | get, set | The radius of the rounded corners at 96 dpi (scaled with the screen); 8 by default, 0 gives square corners. |


## CheckBox

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.CheckBox` - based on `CheckBox`

A themed `CheckBox`, drawn entirely by the library: a rounded box, a checkmark (a dash when undetermined) and the label. The filled box takes its colors from a `UIColorSet` - neutral gray by default, the accent for the primary one - and, like a button, the box has a look for hovered, pressed, focused (shown once the keyboard is used) and disabled. Get one through `UIStyles.CheckBoxes`.

Made by `UIStyles.CheckBoxes` (see the end of this file).

Ignored standard properties (drawn the library's way): `TextAlign`, `RightToLeft`, `Appearance`, `Image`, `ImageAlign`, `TextImageRelation`, `FlatStyle`, `FlatAppearance`, `AutoEllipsis`, `Padding`, `UseVisualStyleBackColor`.

CheckAlign puts the box on the right with TopRight, MiddleRight or BottomRight (the box is always centered vertically). AutoSize = true makes the size follow Text and Font; the factories leave it off.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the filled box: its fill at rest, hovered and pressed, and the mark on each. Left null, the box is filled in the neutral gray (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Gray`); `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. |


## ComboBox

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ComboBox` - based on `ComboBox`

A themed `ComboBox`. The rows of the list are drawn by the library (the selected or hovered one in the neutral gray or in a color set), and so is the closed box of a drop-down list: border, text and arrow, with a look for hovered, dropped down, disabled and keyboard focus (a dotted frame once the keyboard is used; a box that has the focus after a pick with the mouse looks like any other). Get one through `UIStyles.ComboBoxes`.

Made by `UIStyles.ComboBoxes` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the box: the selected (hovered) row of the list, and for the closed box the border when hovered and dropped down (the open list's frame has the latter). Left null, the neutral gray (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Gray`) for the closed box and the gray of the selection in other controls for the row; `UIStyles.ComboBoxes.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. |
| `ReleaseFocusOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button on something else in the window takes the focus out of the box. On by default. |


## ContextMenuStrip

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ContextMenuStrip` - based on `ContextMenuStrip`

A `ContextMenuStrip` themed to match the rest of ErikwnkWFUI instead of the plain system popup menu: the same clicks, keyboard and items as the standard control, only the look changes. Get one through `UIStyles.ContextMenuStrips`.

Made by `UIStyles.ContextMenuStrips` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#797979` | get, set | The frame of the menu and the border of a check mark's box. Defaults to the neutral outline (3:1 against the menu, as on the other controls), whatever `Colors` is; set it to frame the menu in the accent or any other color. |
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the menu: the hovered item takes the set's hover color and text, an item whose submenu is open the pressed ones; the frame is not part of it (see `BorderColor`). Left null, the neutral gray; `UIStyles.ContextMenuStrips.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. A `SelectionBackColor` set explicitly wins over the set's hover color. |
| `SelectionBackColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Background of a hovered/selected menu item. Defaults to the hover color of `Colors`, or without a set to a fixed, neutral gray (`BorderLight`); set this explicitly to use any color. The menus of the grids, the list view and the tab control set it to follow their own highlight color. |


## DataGridView

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.DataGridView` - based on `ReadOnlyDataGridView`

Adds row adding/deleting, an optional delete-row column, clipboard cut/copy/paste, and a right-click context menu on top of `ReadOnlyDataGridView` - the control to reach for when a grid needs to be editable, not just shown. Genuine WinForms controls throughout (not a thin wrapper around a native Win32 common control the way ListView is), so unlike ListView this needs none of that header-subclassing/WM_PAINT-interception - every visual either class has is reachable through its own style properties.

Made by `UIStyles.DataGridViews` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ShowDeleteRowColumn` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether a small "delete this row" button column is shown, pinned as the rightmost column regardless of what else is added afterward. Off by default - a consumer opts in any time after construction (typically right after adding its own columns). The column's own cells are never selectable (clicking one only ever deletes that row, same as selecting a row and pressing Delete already does) and it's never sortable. Also respects `AllowUserToDeleteRows`: clicking the button does nothing while that's false. |


## FlowLayoutPanel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.FlowLayoutPanel` - based on `FlowLayoutPanel`

The flow layout panel of `UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels`: the standard `FlowLayoutPanel`, drawn without flicker, with the scroll bars in the style of the theme and with an optional frame in the library's color (`BorderStyle`, `BorderColor`). Everything else is the standard control. Named `FlowLayoutPanel` so that it does not clash with the standard class in the files that use both namespaces.

Made by `UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the frame when `BorderStyle` is `FixedSingle` (the system draws it in its own color, which is painted over; of `Fixed3D` only the outer line). Follows the theme (and, on a color, is moved until it is seen against it) until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. There is no frame by default. |


## GroupBox

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.GroupBox` - based on `GroupBox`

A themed `GroupBox`, drawn entirely by the library: a thin rounded frame with the title in a gap of its upper edge. The frame is the quiet line of the theme (and is moved until it is seen on a colored surface); with a `UIColorSet` it takes the color of the set. Get one through `UIStyles.GroupBoxes`.

Made by `UIStyles.GroupBoxes` (see the end of this file).

Ignored standard properties (drawn the library's way): `FlatStyle`, `UseCompatibleTextRendering`, `RightToLeft`.

The surface is the one of the parent; children and layout are those of the standard group box.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the frame: the quiet line of the theme (moved until it is seen against the surface) until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. A `Colors` set colors the frame as long as this is not set by hand. |
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the frame: the `Hover` color of the set, moved just far enough to be seen against the surface. Null (the default) is the quiet line of the theme; `UIStyles.GroupBoxes.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent. Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `TitleColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | The color of the title: the primary text color of the theme until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. (`ForeColor` is not used: it is inherited from the parent and so cannot tell a color chosen for the title from the one of the form.) A disabled box shows it faded. |


## ListBox

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ListBox` - based on `ListBox`

An owner-drawn `ListBox` with per-item icons, optional drag-to-reorder (a drag handle appears on the right of each item), enumeration numbers, and fully overridable item colors - a themed alternative to the native list box for anything beyond plain text rows. Use `TitledListBox` instead if you also want a header bar above the list.

Made by `UIStyles.ListBoxes` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowReorder` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether items can be dragged to reorder them (drag handle on the right of each item) - also controls `AllowDrop`. Not with `MultiColumn`, `Sorted` or a `DataSource`. |
| `BackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | The color behind and below the items (the items have `ItemBackColor`); follows the theme until it is set. |
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the frame (`BorderStyle``FixedSingle`, the default). Left alone it is the neutral gray border color of the theme in every variant, also for a list made with a color set or `CreatePrimary`; set it for a frame in another color (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Green.Hover`, say). |
| `DeselectOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button somewhere else in the window (not on a button, a tool bar or a menu) takes the selection away. On by default. |
| `DisabledBackColor` | `Color` | `#191919` | get, set | Background color for an item where `IsItemDisabled` returns true. (The selected item of a list that is disabled as a whole shows the selection color dimmed.) |
| `DisabledForeColor` | `Color` | `#6E6E6E` | get, set | Text color for an item where `IsItemDisabled` returns true, and for every item of a list that is disabled as a whole. Left alone it is worked out from the background the text is on (light or dark, blended toward it); set to `Empty` to have it worked out again. |
| `DisplayTextProvider` | `Func<object, string>` | - | get, set | Computes each item's display text from the item itself, e.g. `o => ((Track)o).Title`. Takes priority over `DisplayMember`; without it the text is what the standard list box makes of an item (`DisplayMember`, `FormatString`, or `item.ToString()`). |
| `DragHandleColor` | `Color` | `#8C8C8C` | get, set | Color of the drag-handle glyph shown on the right of each item when `AllowReorder` is true. Left alone each item has the handle in a quiet version of its own text color (so it reads on a selected item in any color too); set to a color to have that one on every item, `Empty` to have it worked out again. |
| `DragIndicatorColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Color of the horizontal line shown at the drop position while dragging an item to reorder it. Defaults to a fixed, neutral gray (`BorderLight`), matching this control's own `SelectedBackColor` - set this explicitly (e.g. to `Primary`) for an accent-colored indicator instead. |
| `ForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | The text color of the items (see `ItemForeColor`), as in the standard list box. |
| `HoverBackColor` | `Color` | `#333333` | get, set | Background color of the item currently under the mouse (not shown while the list is disabled or an item is being dragged). Left alone it is the row's own color a little way toward the text color - a step lighter on the dark theme, darker on the light one, so it shows on both (this reads the color of an even row); set to a color to have that one on every row, `Empty` to have it worked out again. |
| `IconProvider` | `Func<object, Image>` | - | get, set | Optional per-item icon, drawn to the left of the display text. |
| `IsItemDisabled` | `Func<object, bool>` | - | get, set | Optional per-item disabled look (grayed out): only how the item is drawn. The item can still be clicked, selected and dragged like any other. Independent of the whole control's own `Enabled`. |
| `ItemBackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | Background color of a normal (not selected/hovered/disabled) item. Odd/even rows alternate between this and a slightly darker shade of it. |
| `ItemForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | Text color of a normal (not selected/disabled) item. The same as `ForeColor`. |
| `ItemHeight` | `int` | `35` | get, set | Row height in pixels. Replaces the inherited `ItemHeight` (so the internal default stays in sync, and a height of 0 is not accepted). |
| `SelectedBackColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | The color of the selection. The selected item shows it as a see-through tint over its row (a gray is stronger than a color, as in `SelectionOverlayColor`, but a little stronger still), the text stays the text of the item. Defaults to a fixed, neutral gray (`BorderLight`), not the current accent. `UIStyles.ListBoxes.CreatePrimary` (or `CreateStandard` with a color set) sets it to the accent (the color of the set), the same split as `SelectionBackColor` and `SelectionOverlayColor`. |
| `SelectedForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | Text color of the selected item. Left alone it is the text color of the other items (the selection is only a tint over the row); set to a color to have another one on the selected item, `Empty` to have the item color again. |
| `ShowEnumeration` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Prefixes each item with its 1-based position ("1.", "2.", ...). |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemsReordered` | `EventHandler` | Raised after a drag-to-reorder moves an item to a new position (see `AllowReorder`). |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `ClearSelected()` | Clears the selection (every selected item) and repaints; does nothing when nothing is selected. Hides (does not override) the inherited `ClearSelected`. |
| `MoveItem(int fromIndex, int toIndex)` | Moves an item to a new index without user drag interaction - does not raise `ItemsReordered`. An index that is not there, or the same one twice, changes nothing. Not for a sorted list (it puts every item in its own place) or one with a `DataSource` (its items cannot be moved): that is an `InvalidOperationException`, before anything is touched. |


## ListView

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ListView` - based on `ListView`

A dark-themed, multi-column ListView (Details view only: the other views - list, small and large icons, tiles - draw nothing, and `CheckBoxes` shows no boxes; group headers keep the system's color). Row selection - click, Ctrl+click, Shift+click, rubber-band drag with auto-scroll - is entirely native, left to `MultiSelect` and `SelectedItems`. Only the visuals (row/header colors, fonts, the selection overlay) are this control's own. Hovering a cell whose text is wider than its column shows the full text in a tooltip. A click somewhere else in the application clears the selection - except on a button, a tool bar or a menu, which give commands that work on the selection. Ctrl+C copies every selected row as tab-separated columns; Ctrl+Shift+C does the same with a leading row of column names. Both also put an HTML table on the clipboard alongside the plain text, so apps that understand it (Word, Outlook, browsers, Excel, ...) paste an actual table instead of raw tabs. The right-click menu shows "Copy selection"/"Copy all", each with a submenu for the plain action or "As table". Every copy is confirmed with a `ToastForm`.

Made by `UIStyles.ListViews` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowColumnReordering` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Master switch for whether any column can be dragged to reorder at all. `SetColumnReorderable` still applies per column among whichever this allows; false overrides everything. Defaults to true. |
| `AllowColumnResizing` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Master switch for whether any column can be resized at all. `SetColumnResizable` still applies per column among whichever this allows; false overrides everything. Defaults to true. |
| `AllowSelection` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a row can be selected (by the mouse or the keyboard). True by default; a list that only shows its rows can turn it off, so a click does not highlight anything. |
| `AutoSizeToContent` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the list is as big as its content: as wide as its columns and as high as the header and its items, so it grows and shrinks with them. `MaximumSize` (a width or a height above 0) limits it; what does not fit then scrolls, and the scroll bar gets the room it needs on top of the content (a vertical one makes the list wider, a horizontal one higher, as far as the maximum allows), so it never covers part of the content. Off by default. `FixedRowCount` overrules it. |
| `BackColor` | `Color` | `#141414` | get, set | The color behind and below the rows; follows the theme until it is set. |
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | Color of each column header cell's own border. Defaults to `BorderMedium` regardless of the current accent; `CreatePrimary` sets this to `Primary` instead. |
| `ColumnReorderIndicatorColor` | `Color` | `#B4B4B4` | get, set | Color of the line shown while dragging a column to reorder it. Defaults to a fixed neutral gray, same pattern as `SelectionOverlayColor`. Column reordering is hand-rolled instead of using `AllowColumnReorder`, since the native drag line is comctl32 chrome with no way to recolor or reliably intercept. |
| `ContextMenuSelectionColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Background of a hovered/selected item in this ListView's own right-click context menu. Defaults to a fixed neutral gray, matching `ContextMenuStrip`'s own CreateStandard default; `CreatePrimary` sets this to `Primary` instead, same pattern as `BorderColor`. |
| `CopyConfirmation` | `CopyConfirmationStyle` | `Toast` | get, set | How a Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Shift+C copy is confirmed. Defaults to `Toast` (unchanged from before this existed). |
| `DeselectOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button somewhere else in the window (not on a button, a tool bar or a menu) takes the selection away. On by default. |
| `FixedRowCount` | `int` | `0` | get, set | The number of rows the list has room for: 0 (the default) is an ordinary list, one that is as big as it is made and scrolls. More than 0 makes it a display: it is exactly as wide as its columns and as high as the header and this many rows, whatever size it is given, so it never needs a scroll bar (a `MaximumSize` still limits it, as it does any control). Everything that does not change that size stays as it is: sorting, reordering the columns, selecting (switch them off with `SortingEnabled`, `AllowColumnReordering` and `AllowSelection` where the list only shows). A column that is made wider makes the list wider (`AllowColumnResizing` keeps them as they are). |
| `HeaderBackColor` | `Color` | `#191919` | get, set | Background color of the column header row. |
| `HeaderFont` | `Font` | - | get, set | Font for the column header row - defaults to a bold version of `Font` if never set. Setting this to a larger size is also the way to make the native header band itself taller (there's no direct "header height" API on the underlying Win32 header control - it sizes itself from its own font metrics, same as row height below). The list holds the font it returns: a font that was set stays the caller's to dispose, one the list made goes with it - do not dispose what is read here. |
| `HeaderForeColor` | `Color` | `#8C8C8C` | get, set | Text color of the column header row. |
| `MaximumSize` | `Size` | - | get, set |  |
| `MinimumColumnWidth` | `int` | `40` | get, set | No column can be resized narrower than this. |
| `RowBackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | Background color of a normal (not selected) row. Odd/even rows alternate between this and a slightly darker shade of it. |
| `RowForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | Text color of a normal (not selected) row. |
| `RowHeight` | `int` | `0` | get, set | Forces every row to this exact height in pixels. Unset (0) lets rows size themselves from `Font` as usual. Implemented via the classic Win32 trick of assigning a 1px-wide, N-tall `SmallImageList` - the native ListView derives its row height from the small image list's height when one is set, since there's no direct row-height API either. Don't also assign a real `SmallImageList` for per-item icons while this is set; the two would fight over the same slot. |
| `SelectionOverlayColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Painted on top of a selected cell instead of replacing its background, so a row's own color (e.g. severity) still shows through. Defaults to translucent gray; `CreatePrimary` sets it to `Selection` for an accent-colored look. |
| `SortingEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether clicking a column header cycles it through ascending, descending, and original item order - mirrors `SortingEnabled`. Defaults to true. Turn a single column off instead via `SetColumnSortable` if only that one shouldn't sort. |
| `ToastColors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the toast that confirms a copy (`Toast`): a color set (one of `UIStyles.Colors.Sets`, `UIStyles.Colors.CreateSet(color)` or a `Color`), null for the neutral gray. Until it is set it follows the look of the list: gray for the standard one, the color of the set of `CreateStandard(colors)`, the accent for `CreatePrimary`. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AutoFitColumnsToContent()` | Sizes every column to fit its current content and header text. Call this again after rebuilding the rows, since content driving the "right" width may have changed. |
| `IsColumnReorderable(int columnIndex)` |  |
| `IsColumnResizable(int columnIndex)` |  |
| `IsColumnSortable(int columnIndex)` |  |
| `SetColumnReorderable(int columnIndex, bool reorderable)` | Per-column override, independent of `AllowColumnReordering` - pins a column in place (e.g. a leading "Time" column) while the rest can still be dragged into a new order. |
| `SetColumnResizable(int columnIndex, bool resizable)` | Per-column override, independent of `MinimumColumnWidth` - locks a column at its current width (e.g. a narrow status column) while others stay resizable. |
| `SetColumnSortable(int columnIndex, bool sortable)` | Configurable per column, independent of `SortingEnabled` - a column can be excluded from sorting (e.g. one showing icons or actions rather than comparable data) while the rest stay sortable. |
| `SetSortComparer(ColumnHeader column, IComparer comparer)` | Registers a custom comparer for a column's header-click sort, replacing the default (the sorted column's own text, compared the same "natural" way Windows Explorer's own file listing does - see CompareItemText/StrCmpLogicalW - so e.g. "Row 2" sorts before "Row 10"). The comparer receives the two `ListViewItem`s being compared, so it can read other SubItems or `Tag` instead of just the sorted column's text. Compare in plain ascending order - this control applies descending itself. Pass `null` to remove a comparer and revert that column to the default. |


## LockableTextBox

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.LockableTextBox` - based on `TextField`

A text box that is locked (read-only) until the user unlocks it: a pencil in the box, at its right end, starts the editing - the box is unlocked, has the focus and has its text selected, and the pencil becomes a check mark - and the check mark or the Enter key accepts what was typed and locks the box again; the Escape key gives the old text back. The F2 key and the Enter key on a locked box start the editing too, so that it can be done with the keyboard alone (the pencil is painted by the box and is not seen by a screen reader). The box keeps its `TabStop` as it is: locked, it can still be reached with the Tab key. Make one with `UIStyles.TextBoxes.CreateLockable`.

Made by `UIStyles.TextBoxes` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `IsLocked` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the box is locked (true by default): read-only, with a pencil. Setting it from code locks or unlocks the box and raises `LockedChanged`, and nothing else: the text stays as it is, and the box does not take the focus (see `BeginEdit`, `AcceptEdit` and `CancelEdit` for what the user's buttons do). |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EditAccepted` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the user has accepted the text with the check mark or the Enter key; the box is locked again then. |
| `EditCancelled` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the user has given up the editing with the Escape key; the old text is back and the box is locked again. |
| `LockedChanged` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the box has been locked or unlocked (by the user or by code). |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AcceptEdit()` | What the check mark does: locks the box with the text that was typed and raises `EditAccepted`. |
| `BeginEdit()` | What the pencil does: unlocks the box, gives it the focus and selects its text. |
| `CancelEdit()` | What the Escape key does: gives the old text back, locks the box and raises `EditCancelled`. |


## MultiPanel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.MultiPanel` - based on `CardPanel`

A panel with several pages, of which one is shown at a time - like the pages of a book. A header on top holds, from left to right: the number of the page ("3/12", off by default), the title of the page and two small arrow buttons to go to the previous and the next page. It is made by `UIStyles.MultiPanels`, as a flat panel or as a card (rounded, with a thin line).

Made by `UIStyles.MultiPanels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayRectangle` | `Rectangle` | - | get | The area for the pages: inside the padding and below the header (and the line of `ShowHeaderLine`). |
| `PageCount` | `int` | `0` | get | The number of pages. |
| `Pages` | `ReadOnlyCollection<MultiPanelPage>` | - | get | The pages, in the order of their addition. |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int` | `-1` | get, set | The index of the page that is shown; -1 while there is no page. The first page added is shown at once. |
| `SelectedPage` | `MultiPanelPage` | - | get | The page that is shown; null while there is no page. |
| `ShowHeaderLine` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether a thin line separates the header from the page (off by default). It has the `BorderColor` of the multi panel, and the page area starts a little lower to leave room for it. |
| `ShowPageCount` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the number of the page is shown at the left of the header, like "3/12" (off by default). |
| `TitleAlignment` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `Left` | get, set | Where the title stands between the page count and the arrows: left (the default), center or right. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectedIndexChanged` | `EventHandler` | Raised when another page is shown. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AddPage(string title)` | Adds a page behind the others and returns it for its controls. The first page added is shown. |
| `Next()` | Shows the next page; nothing happens on the last one. |
| `Previous()` | Shows the previous page; nothing happens on the first one. |
| `RemovePage(MultiPanelPage page)` | Takes a page out of the multi panel (it is not disposed, so it can be added to another control or disposed by the caller). If it was shown, the page that took its place is shown. |


## MultiPanelPage

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.MultiPanelPage` - based on `Panel`

One page of a `MultiPanel`: a transparent panel that fills the page area. Put the controls of the page on it like on any panel; its `Title` is shown in the header of the `MultiPanel` while the page is shown.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | `string` | - | get, set | The title in the header of the `MultiPanel`; the same as `Text`. |


## NumericUpDown

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.NumericUpDown` - based on `NumericUpDown`

The standard `NumericUpDown` with the two arrow fields drawn by the library, in the colors of a `UIColorSet` (the standard control draws them in the system's look, a light block next to a dark field), a frame of the library around the field, and a prefix and a suffix for the number. Everything else is the standard control: the text field, the value, the limits, the keyboard, the mouse wheel and the repeat while an arrow is held.

Made by `UIStyles.NumericUpDowns` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the arrow fields: their fill at rest, hovered, pressed and disabled, and the arrow on each. Left null, the neutral look of the theme: the gray set of the library on a dark theme, pale gray fields with a dark arrow on a light one; `UIStyles.NumericUpDowns.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. |
| `Prefix` | `string` | `""` | get, set | Text shown before the number in the field (for example "$ "); the `Value` stays the plain number. Empty by default. |
| `ReleaseFocusOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button on something else in the window takes the focus out of the box. On by default. |

## Panel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.Panel` - based on `Panel`

The panel of `UIStyles.Panels`: the standard `Panel`, drawn without flicker, with the scroll bars in the style of the theme and with an optional frame in the library's color (`BorderStyle`, `BorderColor`). Everything else - `AutoScroll`, `AutoSize`, `BackgroundImage`, `Padding` - is the standard control. Named `Panel` (not `Panel`) so that it does not clash with the standard class in the files that use both namespaces; the factories hand it back as a `Panel`.

Made by `UIStyles.Panels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the frame when `BorderStyle` is `FixedSingle` (the system draws it in its own color, which is painted over; of `Fixed3D` only the outer line). Follows the theme (and, on a color, is moved until it is seen against it) until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. There is no frame by default. |


## ProgressBar

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ProgressBar` - based on `ProgressBar`

The progress bar of `UIStyles.ProgressBars`. It is the standard `ProgressBar` (`Minimum`, `Maximum`, `Value`, `Step`, `PerformStep`, `Increment` and the `Style`s Blocks, Continuous and Marquee with its `MarqueeAnimationSpeed`), drawn by the library in its colors (the native control ignores them while visual styles are on), with a thin border (`BorderStyle`, `BorderColor`) and a track color of its own (`BackColor`, which may be transparent). Every color can be chosen on its own: the fill (`ForeColor`), the track, the border and the text on the track and on the fill (`TextColor`, `TextOnFillColor`). The status variants fill in a color that follows the value from red over yellow to green. A `Text` and the percentage (`ShowPercentage`) can be written on the bar, each left, centered or right (`TextAlign`, `PercentageAlign`); a text that is too long is cut with an ellipsis or moves (`TextScroll`), and a tooltip shows it whole (`ShowFullTextToolTip`). Right-to-left layouts are not supported (`RightToLeft` is ignored; a `RightToLeftLayout` of the standard control mirrors the window, so the fill then starts on the right). The factories hand it back as a `ProgressBar`.

Made by `UIStyles.ProgressBars` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.ProgressBars.CreateStandard()`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | The color of the track. By default the recessed surface of the theme (it follows a change of the theme). Set a color for another one. `Transparent` - which a `ProgressBar` cannot have itself - makes the bar look transparent: the track takes the color of the panel it lies on, also when that changes (and in both themes). `Empty` gives the default back. Independent of `BorderStyle`. |
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the border (see `BorderStyle`). By default the quiet line of the library for the panel the bar lies on (as the frame of a panel): the gray of the theme, moved only as far as the panel needs to keep it seen (1.5:1); it follows the panel and the theme. Set a color for another one, `Empty` gives the default back. |
| `BorderStyle` | `BorderStyle` | `FixedSingle` | get, set | The thin border around the bar: `FixedSingle` (the default; `Fixed3D` looks the same) or `None`, where the bar has no frame of its own and its edge is the track. Only the border: the color of the track is `BackColor`, which can be transparent. |
| `PercentageAlign` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `Right` | get, set | Where the percentage stands on the bar: left, centered or right (the default); see `TextAlign`. It keeps the room of its widest form ("100 %") when it is drawn apart from the text. |
| `ShowFullTextToolTip` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a tooltip shows the whole `Text` while the mouse is on the bar and the text is cut with an ellipsis or moves (on by default); a text that is shown whole has none. |
| `ShowPercentage` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the value is written on the bar as a percentage ("42%" in English, "42 %" in German; off by default). With a `Text` the text stands on the left and the percentage on the right (see `TextAlign` and `PercentageAlign`). Not in the `Marquee` style, which has no value. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A text written on the bar (for a message about the state, like "Uploading ..."); empty by default. It is in the colors that can be read on the track and on the fill, on whatever fill level the bar has. |
| `TextAlign` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `Left` | get, set | Where the `Text` stands on the bar: left (the default), centered or right. At the same place as the percentage (`PercentageAlign`) both are one text, "Upload – 42%"; at another place they are drawn apart, for instance the text left and the percentage right. |
| `TextColor` | `Color` | `Empty` | get, set | The color of the `Text` and the percentage where they stand on the track. `Empty` (the default) is the one that reads best on the track (4.5:1); a disabled bar has the quiet text color of the library in any case. |
| `TextOnFillColor` | `Color` | `Empty` | get, set | The color of the `Text` and the percentage where they stand on the fill. `Empty` (the default) is the one that reads best on the fill (4.5:1). The text is drawn in both colors, each where it is, so that it can be read at any fill level: choose the two to read on the track and on the fill. |
| `TextScroll` | `LabelScroll` | - | get, set | How a `Text` that is too long for its place moves instead of ending in an ellipsis: `None` (the default: it is cut with "..."), `LabelScroll.BackAndForth()` (to its end, a rest, back) or `LabelScroll.Endless()` - the same values as for a label (speed, pause, direction, separator, pause while the mouse is on the bar). The percentage does not move: it stays where it is, and a text that stood together with it stands apart from it while it moves, the percentage at the right end. The text moves only while it does not fit, the bar is shown and enabled, and Windows lets windows animate (Settings, Accessibility). Several texts (`Texts`) are not supported here: use `Text`. |


## PropertyTable

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.PropertyTable` - based on `UserControl`

A two-column "label: editor" table, grouped into optional labeled sections - typical use is a settings/options panel. Build it up with `AddSection` and `AddRow`; a row can hold more than one editor control side by side via the `PropertyColumn`-based overloads. Both return a `PropertyRow` to hide or disable the row later. The width of the label column is `LabelWidth`, the line at the section headers follows `Colors` (none by default; see `UIStyles.PropertyTables`).

Made by `UIStyles.PropertyTables` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The color of the line at the left edge of each section header: the `Hover` color of the set is the main color (brought to where it is seen against the header). Null (the default) is no line; `UIStyles.PropertyTables.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent; `CreateStandard(colors: ...)` takes a color set or simply a color. The labels, the cells and the controls in them stay as they are (the controls have colors of their own). Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `LabelWidth` | `int` | `130` | get, set | The width of the label column in pixels at 96 dpi (130 by default; scaled to the screen). A label that is longer than this wraps onto more lines; what does not fit the row then is cut, and the whole text is its tooltip. Takes effect at once for the rows that are there. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AddRow(Func<string> labelText, Control[] controls)` | A row whose label follows the language (as `AddSection`), with editors that share the width. |
| `AddRow(Func<string> labelText, PropertyColumn[] columns)` |  |
| `AddRow(string labelText, Control[] controls)` | Adds a row: a label on the left, one or more editor controls sharing the remaining width equally on the right (each gets `Auto` sizing). Use the `AddRow` overload instead if the controls need different widths. The row is 42 pixels high (the overloads with a row height: that high at least), or as high as its highest editor needs; a longer label wraps onto a second line. Returns the handle of the row. |
| `AddRow(string labelText, PropertyColumn[] columns)` | Adds a row with explicit per-column sizing (a column may hold no control) - see `Auto`/`Absolute`/`Percent`. |
| `AddRow(Func<string> labelText, int rowHeight, Control[] controls)` |  |
| `AddRow(Func<string> labelText, int rowHeight, PropertyColumn[] columns)` |  |
| `AddRow(string labelText, int rowHeight, Control[] controls)` |  |
| `AddRow(string labelText, int rowHeight, PropertyColumn[] columns)` |  |
| `AddSection(Func<string> title)` | A section whose title follows the language: `title` is asked now and again each time the language changes (`UIStyles.LanguageChanged`) - for a program's own texts. |
| `AddSection(string title)` | Adds a full-width section header row; the handle can hide or disable it. |
| `ClearRows()` | Removes every row and section, leaving an empty table. The editor controls added via `AddRow` are only detached - `Dispose` is NOT called on them, so they keep whatever state they had (text, selection, checked state, ...) and can be re-added afterward via a fresh AddRow. Handy for rebuilding a table live (e.g. on a language switch, re-adding the same controls with new labels) without losing in-progress editor state; if a caller genuinely wants the old controls gone for good, dispose them explicitly first. Everything the table built itself (labels, cells) is disposed, and the `PropertyRow` handles of the old rows do nothing any more. |


## RadioButton

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.RadioButton` - based on `RadioButton`

A themed `RadioButton`, drawn entirely by the library: a round box with a dot when it is selected, and the label. The selected box takes its colors from a `UIColorSet` - neutral gray by default, the accent for the primary one - and, like a button, the box has a look for hovered, pressed, focused (shown once the keyboard is used) and disabled. Get one through `UIStyles.RadioButtons`.

Made by `UIStyles.RadioButtons` (see the end of this file).

Ignored standard properties (drawn the library's way): `TextAlign`, `RightToLeft`, `Appearance`, `Image`, `ImageAlign`, `TextImageRelation`, `FlatStyle`, `FlatAppearance`, `AutoEllipsis`, `Padding`, `UseVisualStyleBackColor`.

Radio buttons with the same parent are one group; use RadioGroup for one choice across parents. CheckAlign puts the box on the right, as on the check box.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the selected box: its fill at rest, hovered and pressed, and the dot on each. Left null, the box is filled in the neutral gray (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Gray`); `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. |


## ReadOnlyDataGridView

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ReadOnlyDataGridView` - based on `DataGridView`

A themed `DataGridView` for displaying data bound via `DataSource` - just showing rows, with column-header sorting, but no editing (no adding, deleting, cutting, or pasting rows). Reach for `DataGridView` instead - it inherits everything here and adds those - whenever the grid genuinely needs to be editable; this one is deliberately the lighter of the two for a grid that only ever shows data, and sets `ReadOnly` to enforce that by default.

Made by `UIStyles.DataGridViews` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ActionConfirmation` | `CopyConfirmationStyle` | `Toast` | get, set | How a copy, or any of DataGridView's own editing actions (cut, paste, clear, delete rows, insert row), is confirmed - the same three-way choice as `CopyConfirmation` (they share `CopyConfirmationStyle` and the same display logic - see `CopyConfirmationDisplay`), named more broadly here since this control has more than just copying to confirm. Defaults to `Toast`. |
| `AllowColumnReordering` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Master switch for whether ANY column can be dragged to reorder it at all - mirrors `AllowColumnReordering`. Per-column overrides via `SetColumnReorderable` still apply among whichever columns this allows; setting this false overrides all of them. Defaults to true. |
| `AllowColumnResizing` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Master switch for whether ANY column can be resized by dragging its header border - mirrors `AllowColumnResizing`. Per-column overrides via `SetColumnResizable` still apply among whichever columns this allows; setting this false overrides all of them. Defaults to true. |
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | Color of each column header cell's own border only - the gridlines BETWEEN data cells (this control's own `GridColor`) stay a fixed neutral color regardless, so `CreatePrimary` doesn't turn every row separator into a wash of accent color too. There used to also be a hand-drawn outer frame around the whole control following this same color, but a real, native in-place editing control (a child window, always on top of anything this control's own OnPaint draws) sitting at a grid edge - the first/last row or column - hid it completely while editing that cell, with no way to draw around a window that's actually there; removed rather than left broken. Only ListView's equivalent `BorderColor` drives both its frame and its header cell dividers with one color, since ListView never draws anything resembling gridlines between actual rows in the first place. Defaults to `BorderMedium` - a fixed, neutral border regardless of the current accent, matching this control's original, unconditional look (`CreateStandard`/ `CreateReadOnlyStandard` still get exactly that, unchanged). `CreatePrimary` sets this to `Primary` instead, the same way ListView's own CreatePrimary does. |
| `ColumnReorderIndicatorColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Color of the vertical line the header shows while a column is being dragged to reorder it. Defaults to a fixed, neutral gray (`BorderLight`), not the current accent - same pattern as `SelectionBackColor` and ListView's own ColumnReorderIndicatorColor. |
| `ContextMenuSelectionColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Background of a hovered/selected item in this grid's own right-click context menu. Defaults to a fixed neutral gray, matching `ContextMenuStrip`'s own CreateStandard default; the factories' CreatePrimary variants set this to `Primary` instead, same pattern as `BorderColor`. |
| `DeselectOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button somewhere else in the window (not on a button, a tool bar or a menu) takes the selection away. On by default; a grid whose cell is being edited keeps its selection. |
| `HeaderBackColor` | `Color` | `#191919` | get, set | Background color of the column header row. |
| `HeaderForeColor` | `Color` | `#8C8C8C` | get, set | Text color of the column header row. |
| `MinimumColumnWidth` | `int` | `40` | get, set | No column can be resized narrower than this - mirrors `MinimumColumnWidth`. Whichever of this or the column's own native `MinimumWidth` is larger actually applies. |
| `RowBackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | Background color of a normal (not selected) row. Odd/even rows alternate between this and a slightly darker shade of it. |
| `RowForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | Text color of a normal (not selected) row. |
| `SelectionBackColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Background color of a selected cell/row. Defaults to a fixed, neutral gray (`BorderLight`), not the current accent - `CreatePrimary`/ `CreateReadOnlyPrimary` set this to `Primary` explicitly instead, same pattern as ListView's SelectionOverlayColor. |
| `ShowEnumeration` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether an optional "#" row-number column is shown, pinned as the LEFTMOST column regardless of what else is added afterward - the mirror image of `ShowDeleteRowColumn`'s own rightmost pinning. Off by default - a consumer opts in any time after construction. Each row's number is always its CURRENT position (1-based, top to bottom): sorting, inserting, or deleting rows renumbers automatically. The column IS sortable (unlike the delete column) - clicking it sorts by whatever position each row held right before the click, so ascending is a no-op (already in that order), descending reverses the current row order, and a third click restores the original bind order, same as any other column's cycle. Its width is fixed (not user-resizable, matching the delete column), but automatically wide enough for however many digits the current row count needs - 150 rows gets a column sized for "150", not padded for some arbitrary maximum. |
| `SortingEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether clicking a column header cycles it through ascending, descending, and original row order (see the "Column header sorting" remarks on `CycleSort`). Defaults to true; a consumer sets this to false - any time before rows are bound, since `OnColumnAdded` reads it once per column - to keep headers as plain labels for a grid where reordering rows wouldn't make sense. Clicking a header still clears a stray selection either way (see `HandleMouseDown`); only the sorting itself is affected. The glyph/arrow shown for the active sort column is always this control's own concern, not something a consumer sets. |
| `ToastColors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the toast that confirms an action (`Toast`): a color set (one of `UIStyles.Colors.Sets`, `UIStyles.Colors.CreateSet(color)` or a `Color`), null for the neutral gray. Until it is set it follows the look of the grid: gray for the standard one, the color of the set of the factories' `colors`, the accent for `CreatePrimary`. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `IsColumnReorderable(int columnIndex)` |  |
| `IsColumnResizable(int columnIndex)` | Mirrors `IsColumnResizable` - see `AllowColumnResizing`/`SetColumnResizable`. |
| `SetColumnReorderable(int columnIndex, bool reorderable)` | Configurable per column, independent of `AllowColumnReordering`: a column can be pinned in place (e.g. `DataGridView`'s own delete-row column, always pinned rightmost) while the rest can still be freely dragged into a new order. |
| `SetColumnResizable(int columnIndex, bool resizable)` | Configurable per column, independent of `AllowColumnResizing`: a column can be locked at its current width entirely (e.g. `DataGridView`'s own delete-row column) while the rest can still be freely resized. Mirrors `SetColumnResizable`. |
| `SetSortComparer(DataGridViewColumn column, IComparer comparer)` | Registers a custom comparer for a specific column, used by column-header sorting (see `SortingEnabled`/ `CycleSort`) instead of the default comparison (`IComparable`, falling back to case-insensitive string comparison) - useful for a column whose cell values don't sort correctly as plain strings/IComparables on their own, e.g. dates stored in a non-lexicographic text format, or numbers stored as strings. The comparer receives the two cells' raw `Value` objects and is expected to compare them in plain ascending order - this control still applies ascending/descending itself, the same way it already does for the default comparison, so a registered comparer never needs to know which direction is currently active. Pass `null` as `comparer` to remove one and revert that column to the default. Set any time after the column exists; not tied to binding order the way `SortingEnabled` is. |


## ReadOnlyTabControl

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ReadOnlyTabControl` - based on `TabControl`

A themed, display-only `TabControl`: the user can switch tabs but not add or close them. Behaves exactly like the standard control (same `TabPages`, keyboard handling, alignment, multiline rows, images, events) - only the drawing is replaced with the library's own look. `TabControl` builds on this and adds a right-click menu to add, rename and close tabs.

Made by `UIStyles.TabControls` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowSelectingDisabledTabs` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a tab whose page is disabled can be selected. On by default, like the standard control, where a disabled page can still be opened (its content is disabled, the tab is not). Off: a click, the keyboard or code cannot select such a tab, and the arrow keys and Ctrl+Tab skip over it. A tab that is selected when its page gets disabled stays selected. |
| `Appearance` | `TabAppearance` | `Normal` | get, set | Always `Normal` - this control only draws tabs, never button-style tabs. Setting anything else throws. |
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | Color of the tab outlines and the border around the page area. |
| `DisabledTabForeColor` | `Color` | `#6E6E6E` | get, set | Text color of a tab whose page is disabled. |
| `HeaderBackColor` | `Color` | `Transparent` | get, set | Background behind the tabs, where no tab is drawn. Transparent by default, so the parent shows through and only the tabs and the page box are visible. |
| `HoverTabBackColor` | `Color` | `#323232` | get, set | Background of the tab under the mouse. Only used while `HotTrack` is on - which it is by default here, unlike the standard control. By default a dark theme lightens a hovered tab (`BackgroundLight`) and a light theme steps it toward the selected tab from the dark side (`BackgroundDarkElevated`), so a hovered tab never looks more selected than the selected one. |
| `PageBackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | Background color of the pages, applied to pages that don't have a color of their own - existing ones and ones added later. A page whose `BackColor` was set individually keeps it, as with the standard control. |
| `SelectedTabBackColor` | `Color` | `#232323` | get, set | Background of the selected tab. Defaults to the same color as `PageBackColor` so the tab flows into its page. |
| `SelectedTabForeColor` | `Color` | `#F0F0F0` | get, set | Text color of the selected tab. |
| `SelectedTabIndicatorColor` | `Color` | `#8C8C8C` | get, set | Color of the bar on the outer edge of the selected tab. Defaults to a neutral gray (`TextTertiary`, which stands out from the tab in both themes), not the current accent - set it to `PrimaryLight` for an accent-colored bar, which is what `UIStyles.TabControls.CreatePrimary` does. |
| `TabBackColor` | `Color` | `#141414` | get, set | Background of a tab that is neither selected nor hovered. |
| `TabForeColor` | `Color` | `#B4B4B4` | get, set | Text color of a tab that is not selected. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TabRightClick` | `EventHandler<TabRightClickEventArgs>` | Raised when the right mouse button goes down on a tab - with the page, its index and where in the control the click was. The standard control has no such event; it is what a custom menu or the `TabControl`'s add/close menu builds on. |


## ScrollingLabel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ScrollingLabel` - based on `Label`

The label of the library, made by `UIStyles.Labels`: the standard `Label` in the colors of the library, with a text that can move when it is too long for the label: back and forth or endlessly (`ScrollMode`, `Scroll`).

Made by `UIStyles.Labels` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Labels.CreateStandard()`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ForeColor` | `Color` | `#B4B4B4` | get, set |  |
| `Scroll` | `LabelScroll` | - | get, set | All of the above in one value: set to take over every setting at once (the movement starts over once), read to get the settings the label has now. Null is no movement. |
| `ScrollDirection` | `LabelScrollDirection` | `Left` | get, set | Which way the text moves in the endless mode: to the left (the default) or to the right. Back and forth always starts to the left. |
| `ScrollMode` | `LabelScrollMode` | `None` | get, set | Whether and how a text that is too long for the label moves instead of ending in an ellipsis: not at all (the default), back and forth with a rest at both ends, or endlessly in one direction. A text that fits stands still. It applies to a text of one line in a label that is enabled; a disabled label shows the start of the text with an ellipsis. A label with `AutoSize` is as big as its text, so back and forth does not move it; endless does, and the size of the label stays what AutoSize makes it (a label with a maximum width wraps its text and does not move). With several texts (`Texts`) AutoSize is not of much use: the label is as wide as all the texts together, so there is little left to move. While the text moves it starts at the left whatever `TextAlign` says (the vertical place is kept), and right-to-left is not supported (as everywhere in the library). An image of the label is not shown while the text moves, only while it stands still. |
| `ScrollPause` | `LabelScrollPause` | `Medium` | get, set | How long the text rests at the start and at the end when it moves back and forth: a short time, a medium one (the default) or a long one. |
| `ScrollPauseOnHover` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the moving text stands still while the mouse is on the label, so that it can be read. Off by default. |
| `ScrollSeparator` | `LabelScrollSeparator` | `Dot` | get, set | The sign between the end of the text and its next appearance in the endless mode: a dot (the default), a bar, a diamond or none. |
| `ScrollSpeed` | `LabelScrollSpeed` | `Medium` | get, set | How fast the moving text moves: slowly, at a medium speed (the default) or fast. |
| `ShowFullTextToolTip` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a tooltip shows the whole text while the mouse is on the label and the text moves because it is too long for the label (on by default). A text that fits has none, and neither has one that does not move (a standard label with `AutoEllipsis` has a tooltip of its own). |


## SlimProgressBar

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.SlimProgressBar` - based on `Control`

A thin, fully custom-drawn progress bar for slim status-strip-style indicators (a background task's progress as a thin strip under a status label), see `UIStyles.SlimProgressBars`; `UIStyles.ProgressBars` is the prominent, full-size one. It is a plain control, with no native progress bar underneath. Every color can be chosen on its own: the fill (`ForeColor`), the track (`BackColor`) and the text (`TextColor`). It offers what the standard `ProgressBar` does: `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `Value`, `Step`, `PerformStep`, `Increment` and the `Style`s Blocks, Continuous (the default) and Marquee with its `MarqueeAnimationSpeed`. One difference: a `Value` outside the range is limited to it instead of throwing, and a range may contain negative numbers (the standard control refuses a negative `Minimum`). Right-to-left layouts are not supported (`RightToLeft` is ignored). A `Text` (a message about the state) and the `ShowPercentage` are written next to the strip, at the `TextPosition`; the strip itself stays as thin as it is. A text that is too long is cut with an ellipsis or moves (`TextScroll`), and a tooltip shows it whole (`ShowFullTextToolTip`).

Made by `UIStyles.SlimProgressBars` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BackColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the track. By default the quiet line of the library for the panel the bar lies on (as the frame of a panel): the gray of the theme, moved only as far as the panel needs to keep the track seen (1.5:1) - the track has no border of its own here. It follows the panel and the theme. Set a color for another one, `Empty` gives the default back; a transparent color is the one of the panel. |
| `ForeColor` | `Color` | `ControlText` | get, set | The color of the fill. The bars of `UIStyles.SlimProgressBars` have the main color of their color set (or the gray) until one is set; that color is moved only as far as needed to stand out from the track (3:1), a color set here is used as it is. `Empty` gives the default back. |
| `MarqueeAnimationSpeed` | `int` | `100` | get, set | The time in milliseconds between two steps of the marquee (100 by default); 0 stops it. |
| `Maximum` | `int` | `100` | get, set | The upper end of the range (100 by default). A `Value` above it is lowered to it. |
| `Minimum` | `int` | `0` | get, set | The lower end of the range (0 by default); it may be negative. A `Value` below it is raised to it. |
| `PercentageAlign` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `Right` | get, set | Where the percentage stands in its line above or below the strip: right (the default), centered or left; see `TextAlign`. It keeps the room of its widest form ("100 %") when it is drawn apart from the text. |
| `ShowFullTextToolTip` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a tooltip shows the whole `Text` while the mouse is on the bar and the text is cut with an ellipsis or moves (on by default); a text that is shown whole has none. |
| `ShowPercentage` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the value is written as a percentage ("42%" in English, "42 %" in German; off by default), at the `TextPosition`. Above and below the bar it stands on the right, with the `Text` on the left; at the sides both are one text: "Upload – 42%". Not in the `Marquee` style, which has no value. |
| `Step` | `int` | `10` | get, set | How much `PerformStep` adds to `Value` (10 by default, as in the standard control). |
| `Style` | `ProgressBarStyle` | `Continuous` | get, set | How the fill looks: `Continuous` (the default), `Blocks`, or `Marquee` - a block that runs through the bar again and again, for an action whose duration is not known (`Value` does not matter then). |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A text (for a message about the state, like "Uploading ..."); empty by default. Without a text and without the percentage the control is only the strip, as thin as it was made. With one, its preferred size (for `AutoSize`) takes the text line, or the width of the text at the sides; a size that was set stays. |
| `TextAlign` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `Left` | get, set | Where the `Text` stands in its line above or below the strip: left (the default), centered or right. At the same place as the percentage (`PercentageAlign`) both are one text, "Upload – 42%"; at another place they are drawn apart (by default the text on the left and the percentage on the right). At the sides of the strip there is one text that has just its room, so neither of the two alignments does anything there. |
| `TextColor` | `Color` | `Empty` | get, set | The color of the `Text` and the percentage, which stand on the panel next to the strip. `Empty` (the default) is the one that reads best on that panel (4.5:1); a disabled bar has the quiet text color of the library in any case. |
| `TextPosition` | `SlimProgressBarTextPosition` | `Above` | get, set | Where the `Text` and the percentage are placed: `Above` (the default), below, left or right of the bar. |
| `TextScroll` | `LabelScroll` | - | get, set | How a `Text` that is too long for its place moves instead of ending in an ellipsis: `None` (the default: it is cut with "..."), `LabelScroll.BackAndForth()` (to its end, a rest, back) or `LabelScroll.Endless()`, the same values as for a label (speed, pause, direction, separator, pause while the mouse is on the bar). The percentage does not move: it stays where it is, and a text that stood together with it stands apart from it while it moves, the percentage at the right end. The text moves only while it does not fit, while the bar is shown and enabled, and while Windows lets windows animate (Settings, Accessibility); several texts (`Texts`) are not supported here, use `Text`. |
| `UseStatusGradient` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | When true, the fill color follows `Value` instead of `ForeColor` - red at `Minimum`, yellow at the midpoint, green at `Maximum`, blending smoothly between them. For a "status/health" bar where the color itself communicates good/bad, not just the fill amount. |
| `Value` | `int` | `0` | get, set | The current value. One outside the range is limited to it instead of throwing (the standard control throws). |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Increment(int value)` | Adds `value` (it can be negative) to `Value`, limited to `Minimum` and `Maximum`. Like the standard control, it throws while the `Style` is Marquee. |
| `PerformStep()` | Adds `Step` to `Value`, limited to `Minimum` and `Maximum`. Like the standard control, it throws while the `Style` is Marquee (there is no value then). |


## Spinner

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.Spinner` - based on `Control`

A loading spinner: an arc that turns over a faint full ring (the load is unknown), or, with `IsIndeterminate` off, a ring that fills up to the `Value` (the load is known). Fully custom-drawn, follows the theme, transparent background. The arc turns while `IsSpinning` is set and the control is shown and enabled and Windows lets windows animate (a spinner on a hidden window only looks four times a second whether it is shown again); `Speed` says how fast, and `HideWhenStopped` hides the ring while it does not. A `Text` stands next to the ring (at the `TextPosition`), and `ShowPercentage` writes the `Value` in its centre. The color of the arc is `ArcColor` if set, else, with `UseStatusGradient`, red over yellow to green by the `Value`, else the main color of `Colors` (a color set) or the neutral gray; a disabled spinner is in the disabled color. The `UIStyles.Spinners` factories preset these. For a screen reader it is a progress bar: the text is its name and, for a known load, the percentage its value. Right-to-left layouts are not supported (`RightToLeft` is ignored).

Made by `UIStyles.Spinners` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ArcColor` | `Color` | `Empty` | get, set | An explicit color of the arc, overriding `Colors` and `UseStatusGradient` (not the disabled look). `Empty` (the default) uses those rules. |
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the arc: its main color is the `Hover` color of the set (Green is the usual green, the primary set the accent). Null (the default) is the neutral gray; `UIStyles.Spinners.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent. `ArcColor` and `UseStatusGradient` win over it. Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `HideWhenStopped` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | True = the ring is not drawn while `IsSpinning` is false (the `Text` stays); false (the default) = the ring stands still where it is. |
| `IsIndeterminate` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | True (the default) = the load is unknown: an arc of fixed length turns. False = the load is known: the arc is as long as the `Value` (from the top, clockwise) and stands still. |
| `IsSpinning` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the arc turns (true by default). False stands it still where it is, e.g. while nothing is loading; with `HideWhenStopped` the ring is gone then. It also stands still while the control is disabled or while Windows has the animations switched off (the ring stays visible then). A known load (`IsIndeterminate` off) never turns. |
| `ShowPercentage` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the `Value` is written (bold, as a number) in the centre of the ring (off by default). The digits scale to the ring, with the size of "100" so that they do not change while the number counts up; in a ring too small for them (below about 30 px) they are left out. `UIStyles.Spinners.CreateProgress*` make a ring of 40 px. |
| `Speed` | `SpinnerSpeed` | `Medium` | get, set | How fast the arc turns (a turn in about 1.2 seconds by default, the same on every computer). It has no effect on a known load. |
| `Text` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A text next to the ring (empty by default: only the ring). Make the control as wide as ring and text need - the ring is a circle as high as the control (with the text left or right of it) or as large as the room left by the text (above or below it), and a text that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis. A screen reader reads it as the name. |
| `TextPosition` | `SpinnerTextPosition` | `Right` | get, set | Where the `Text` stands in relation to the ring (right of it by default). |
| `Thickness` | `int` | `0` | get, set | Stroke width in pixels. 0 (the default) scales it to the size of the control (an eighth, at least 2 px). |
| `UseStatusGradient` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | True = the arc color tells the state of the load: a solid color blended red (0) over yellow to green (100) by `Value`. Ignored when `ArcColor` is set. As `UseStatusGradient`. |
| `Value` | `int` | `0` | get, set | The load, as a percentage from 0 to 100 (a value outside is limited to it; 0 by default). It colors the arc with `UseStatusGradient`, is written in the centre with `ShowPercentage`, is the length of the arc with `IsIndeterminate` off and then also the value for a screen reader. |


## TabControl

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TabControl` - based on `ReadOnlyTabControl`

A `ReadOnlyTabControl` whose user can also add, rename and close tabs, through a right-click menu in the library's own design.

Made by `UIStyles.TabControls` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowUserToAddTabs` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Lets the user add tabs from the right-click menu. On by default. |
| `AllowUserToCloseTabs` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Lets the user close tabs from the right-click menu - never the last one. On by default. |
| `AllowUserToRenameTabs` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Lets the user rename tabs - from the right-click menu and, see `RenameTabOnDoubleClick`, by double-clicking. On by default. |
| `ContextMenuSelectionColor` | `Color` | `#5A5A5A` | get, set | Selection color of the built-in right-click menu. Defaults to a neutral gray (`BorderLight`); the Primary factory sets it to the accent, same as on `ContextMenuSelectionColor`. |
| `IsRenamingTab` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether a tab's name is being edited right now. |
| `MaxTabNameLength` | `int` | `40` | get, set | The most characters a tab name can have when the user types it - the rename box stops accepting more, and a pasted text is cut to fit. 40 by default; must be at least 1. Names that are already longer are left as they are until they are edited. |
| `RenameTabAfterAdding` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether a tab added from the menu starts out in rename mode, so it can be named right away. Off by default. |
| `RenameTabOnDoubleClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a double-click on a tab starts renaming it (needs `AllowUserToRenameTabs`). On by default. |
| `SelectTabOnRightClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a right-click on a tab selects it, so it is visible which tab the menu acts on. On by default; switch it off for the standard control's behavior, where only a left-click selects. |
| `ShowLockIcon` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a tab that was locked against renaming or closing (with `SetTabRenamable` / `SetTabClosable`) shows a small padlock in front of its name, and a tooltip saying what is locked. On by default. The room for the padlock is only reserved while the control's own `ImageList` is not in use; with one of yours, the padlock sits at the right end of the tab instead. Assign your own `ImageList` before locking tabs: tabs that were locked first have taken an image index of the control's own list, which would then point into yours. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TabAdding` | `EventHandler<TabAddingEventArgs>` | Raised before a tab is added from the context menu. Cancel it, or replace `TabPage` to add a different page. |
| `TabClosing` | `EventHandler<TabClosingEventArgs>` | Raised before a tab is closed from the context menu. Cancel it to keep the tab. |
| `TabRenameStarting` | `EventHandler<TabRenameStartingEventArgs>` | Raised when a rename is about to start - and also when the control only checks whether one would be allowed, to enable or disable the menu entry. Cancel it to keep that tab's name from being edited. |
| `TabRenamed` | `EventHandler<TabRenamedEventArgs>` | Raised after a tab got its new name. |
| `TabRenaming` | `EventHandler<TabRenamingEventArgs>` | Raised before a typed name is applied to a tab. Cancel it to keep the old name, or change `NewName`. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `BeginRenameTab(int index)` | Turns the name of a tab into a text box: type the new name, Enter or leaving the box applies it, Escape drops it. The tab is selected first. Returns whether the edit started - it does not without `AllowUserToRenameTabs`, for a tab that was locked with `SetTabRenamable` or vetoed through `TabRenameStarting`. |
| `IsTabClosable(TabPage tabPage)` | Whether `SetTabClosable` allows closing this tab. Says nothing about the control-wide switch or the last-tab rule. |
| `IsTabRenamable(TabPage tabPage)` | Whether `SetTabRenamable` allows renaming this tab. Says nothing about the control-wide switch or `TabRenameStarting`. |
| `SetTabClosable(TabPage tabPage, bool closable)` | Allows or forbids the user to close one tab, on top of `AllowUserToCloseTabs` (which forbids it for all). A tab is closable until this says otherwise - though never the last one left. |
| `SetTabRenamable(TabPage tabPage, bool renamable)` | Allows or forbids the user to rename one tab, on top of `AllowUserToRenameTabs` (which forbids it for all). A tab is renamable until this says otherwise. |


## TableLayoutPanel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TableLayoutPanel` - based on `TableLayoutPanel`

The table layout panel of `UIStyles.TableLayoutPanels`: the standard `TableLayoutPanel`, drawn without flicker, with the scroll bars in the style of the theme, with an optional frame in the library's color (`BorderStyle`, `BorderColor`) and with the lines of `CellBorderStyle.Single` in colors of the library (`CellBorderColor`, `InnerCellBorderColor`, `OuterCellBorderColor`) of which the ones to show can be chosen (`CellBorderLines`). Everything else is the standard control. Named `TableLayoutPanel` so that it does not clash with the standard class in the files that use both namespaces.

Made by `UIStyles.TableLayoutPanels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the frame when `BorderStyle` is `FixedSingle` (the system draws it in its own color, which is painted over; of `Fixed3D` only the outer line). Follows the theme (and, on a color, is moved until it is seen against it) until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. There is no frame by default. |
| `CellBorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the lines around and between the cells when `CellBorderStyle` is `Single` (the system draws them in its own color, which is painted over; the other styles are left to the system). Follows the theme (and, on a color, is moved until it is seen against it) until it is set; `Empty` gives that back. `InnerCellBorderColor` and `OuterCellBorderColor` take other colors for one kind of line. There are no lines by default. |
| `CellBorderLines` | `CellBorderLines` | `All` | get, set | Which of the lines of `CellBorderStyle``Single` are shown: all of them (the default), only the ones around the whole table, or only the ones between the cells. The lines that are not shown leave an empty pixel in their place (the layout does not change), painted in the background of the table or - with a transparent table - of what lies behind it. A background image is not repainted there. |
| `InnerCellBorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the lines between the cells. Left empty (the default) it is the `CellBorderColor`, also when that changes; `Empty` gives that back. |
| `OuterCellBorderColor` | `Color` | `#464646` | get, set | The color of the lines around the whole table (the outer edge of the cells; not the frame of `BorderStyle`). Left empty (the default) it is the `CellBorderColor`, also when that changes; `Empty` gives that back. |


## TextField

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TextField` - based on `TextBox`

The text box of the library: the standard `TextBox` with the frame of the library (a quiet outline, and with the focus the color of `Colors`) instead of the system's, a placeholder that is painted and never is the text, a slightly dimmed background while it is read-only, and a tooltip with the whole text when the text is wider than the box (`ToolTipWhenCut`). Make one with `UIStyles.TextBoxes`; the factories give the standard type, except `CreateLockable`, which gives a `LockableTextBox`. The box can have a button at its right end, inside the frame (the pencil of a `LockableTextBox`, the eye of a password box): it is painted by the box, so it is not a control of its own and not seen by a screen reader - what it does can also be done with the keyboard (see `LockableTextBox`). The class has its own name, as `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TextBox` would be ambiguous in every file that uses both namespaces.

Made by `UIStyles.TextBoxes` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The color of the frame while the box has the focus: the `Hover` color of the set is the main color (brought to where it is seen against the field). Null (the default) is the text color of the field; `UIStyles.TextBoxes.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent; `CreateStandard(colors: ...)` takes a color set or simply a color. The fill and the text stay those of the theme. Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `Placeholder` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A hint that is shown in the muted color while the box is empty and has not the focus (as the placeholder of a web page); it is painted over the box and never is its `Text`. Empty (the default) is none. |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string` | `""` | get, set | The `PlaceholderText` of the standard box (.NET 5 and later) is the `Placeholder` of this one: code that sets it gets the hint of the library (in the colors of the theme, where a text would stand) instead of the system's, which is drawn in a gray of its own. |
| `ReleaseFocusOnOutsideClick` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether a click with the left mouse button on something else in the window takes the focus out of the box. On by default. |
| `ToolTipWhenCut` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the whole text is shown as a tooltip while the mouse is over the box and the text is wider than the box (true by default). Not while the box hides what is typed (a password that is not shown), and not for a multi-line box, which shows its text. |
