## ToggleSwitch

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ToggleSwitch` - based on `Control`

An iOS-style on/off switch, an alternative to a `CheckBox`. Make one with `UIStyles.ToggleSwitches`: gray when it is on (`CreateStandard`), in the accent (`CreatePrimary`) or in the colors of a color set (`colors:`). It works as a standard check box does: a click toggles it when the press ends over it, the space bar toggles it (pressed while down, toggled on release, with a focus frame once the keyboard has been used), and a screen reader is told a check button with its state - set `AccessibleName`, as there is no text on the switch. When the user switches it, the knob glides (not when code sets `Checked`, nor while Windows has the animations off). It follows the theme and the dpi of the screen. There is no `Text` (put a label beside it), no three states and no right-to-left layout.

Made by `UIStyles.ToggleSwitches` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Checked` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | The switch's on/off state. |
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the switch while it is on: the `Hover` color of the set is the main color (the track, its outline and the outline while the mouse is over it); it is moved just far enough to stand out from the surface and from the white knob. Null (the default) is a neutral gray; `UIStyles.ToggleSwitches.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent; `CreateStandard(colors: ...)` takes a color set or simply a color (e.g. a red one for a switch that is always a danger). Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `ToolTipText` | `string` | - | get, set | Write-only shorthand for setting both `ToolTipTextChecked` and `ToolTipTextUnchecked` to the same text. |
| `ToolTipTextChecked` | `string` | `""` | get, set | Tooltip text shown while `Checked` is true. |
| `ToolTipTextUnchecked` | `string` | `""` | get, set | Tooltip text shown while `Checked` is false. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckedChanged` | `EventHandler` | Raised when `Checked` changes, whether from user interaction or setting the property directly. |


## TrackBar

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TrackBar` - based on `Control`

A slim, theme-matching horizontal slider: the library's version of the WinForms `TrackBar`, fully custom-drawn. The `Value` runs from `Minimum` (0 by default) to `Maximum` (1 by default) and is a fraction, not a whole number. The mouse drags the thumb (a press on the thumb takes hold of it where it was pressed, a press on the track puts it there), and the keys (arrows by `SmallChange`, Page Up and Down by `LargeChange`, Home and End to the ends) and the mouse wheel work as on the original. `ValueChanged` fires on every change from the user (drag, click on the track, keys, wheel); unlike the original it does not fire when `Value` is set from code, so that code which keeps the slider up to date cannot start a loop. The filled part and the thumb are gray, the color of `Colors` (a color set or simply a color; `UIStyles.TrackBars.CreatePrimary` follows the accent), moved as far as needed to stand out from what the slider lies on, in both themes. The popup has the same colors unless `ValuePopupColors` says otherwise. `ShowValuePopup` shows the value above the thumb, written as `FormatValue` says (`FormatPercent` for a volume from 0 to 1); a screen reader is told it is a slider and its value. The measures are scaled with the screen. Not offered: tick marks, the vertical orientation, `AutoSize`; right-to-left layouts are not supported (`RightToLeft` is ignored).

Made by `UIStyles.TrackBars` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the filled part and the thumb: the `Hover` color of the set is the main color (Green is the usual green, the primary set the accent). Null (the default) is a neutral gray; `UIStyles.TrackBars.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent; `UIStyles.TrackBars.CreateStandard(colors: ...)` takes a color set or simply a color. The popup has the same colors unless `ValuePopupColors` says otherwise. Not written by the designer (a set is code). |
| `FormatValue` | `Func<double, string>` | - | get, set | How a value is written for the popup and for a screen reader. By default as a number with up to two decimals, the decimal sign by the language of the library (not the culture of the computer); `FormatPercent` writes a value from 0 to 1 as whole percent. Null gives the default back. |
| `IsDragging` | `bool` | `false` | get | True while the user is dragging the thumb - callers can pause external updates. |
| `LargeChange` | `double` | `0.1` | get, set | How far Page Up and Page Down move the value. 0 or less (the default) is a tenth of the range. |
| `Maximum` | `double` | `1` | get, set | The top of the range (1 by default); it is always above `Minimum`. A `Value` above it is lowered to it; not a number and infinity are ignored. |
| `Minimum` | `double` | `0` | get, set | The bottom of the range (0 by default). A `Value` below it is raised to it; not a number and infinity are ignored. |
| `ShowValuePopup` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the value is shown in a small popup above the thumb: while the user drags it, then briefly after they let go, click once or use a key or the wheel, and for as long as the mouse hovers over the slider. Off by default. |
| `SmallChange` | `double` | `0.05` | get, set | How far an arrow key or a step of the mouse wheel moves the value. 0 or less (the default) is a twentieth of the range. |
| `TrackInsetPixels` | `int` | `7` | get | The same in the pixels of the screen this slider is on (more than `TrackInset` where the screen is scaled). |
| `Value` | `double` | `0` | get, set | The value, from `Minimum` to `Maximum` (one outside is limited to it, infinity is the end of the range, not a number is ignored). Setting it from code updates the display without raising `ValueChanged`. |
| `ValuePopupColors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the popup (its background and its text): a color set, or simply a color. Null (the default) gives it the colors of the slider - gray for `CreateStandard`, the accent for `CreatePrimary`, the set of `Colors` - and it follows them. Not written by the designer (a set is code). |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DragEnded` | `EventHandler` | Raised once when a drag ends: the mouse is released, taken away (a dialog, another window) or the slider is disabled. |
| `DragStarted` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the user presses the thumb or the track to begin a drag (before the value follows the mouse). |
| `ValueChanged` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the user changes the value (drag, click on the track, keys, wheel), once for each other value; not when code sets it. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `FormatPercent(double value)` | A value from 0 to 1 as whole percent, written the way of the language of the library ("10%" in English, "10 %" in German): for `FormatValue` of a volume or the like. |


## VersionPanel

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.VersionPanel` - based on `Panel`

A narrow strip with the version of the program at its right end and - while an update is known - a small green button next to it that leads to the update. It is the version strip of a settings window as an element of its own, made by `UIStyles.VersionPanels`: it can be put in any window or page, not only in `AppForm`.

Made by `UIStyles.VersionPanels` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UpdateAvailable` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the update button is there (an update was announced with `ShowUpdate` or found by `CheckForUpdateAsync`). |
| `VersionText` | `string` | `"v15.0.0"` | get, set | The text at the right end; the version of the program ("v1.2.3") until it is set, an empty text shows none. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CheckForUpdateAsync(AppUpdater updater, TimeSpan timeout, Version currentVersion)` | Asks GitHub whether there is a newer version and shows the update button if there is one. Silent: it never shows a message and never throws (no net, a slow answer or no newer version just leave the strip as it is). |
| `HideUpdate()` | Takes the update button away (and disposes it). |
| `ShowUpdate(AppUpdater updater, UpdateCheckResult result, Version currentVersion)` | Shows the update button for an update that is known: a click on it asks the user, downloads and installs the new version (see `ShowUpdatePromptAsync`). A button that was there is replaced. |


## VolumeControl

`ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.VolumeControl` - based on `Panel`

A ready-made volume control for audio: a mute button (a loudspeaker, crossed out while it is muted) with a `TrackBar` beside it, as on video sites. The slider shows the percentage in a popup while it is used (or, with `ShowPercentage`, as a number beside it). It works as the controls of YouTube and Twitch: a click on the button (or the key M on the slider) mutes and, the next time, brings back the volume that was before; moving the slider to 0 mutes, moving it away from 0 turns the sound on again; the mouse wheel over the button turns the volume like the wheel over the slider; while it is muted the slider stands at 0 and the volume is remembered. `Volume` is the level the sound has when it is on, `IsMuted` whether it is off, and `EffectiveVolume` what the audio output is to get (0 while muted). `VolumeChanged` comes when the user changes what is heard, not when code sets `Volume` or `IsMuted` (as the `ValueChanged` of the slider). Make one with `UIStyles.VolumeControls`. The mute button and the slider are reachable for what is not offered here (`MuteButton`, `Slider`: the colors of the popup, the steps of the keys ...); right-to-left layouts are not supported. It makes no sound itself: a player that implements `IAudioVolume` (of ErikwnkCore) is coupled with `Target` - the control sets it, and follows it when it changes by itself.

Made by `UIStyles.VolumeControls` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the slider and its popup (a color set, or simply a color; the mute button has the neutral look). Null (the default) is gray; `UIStyles.VolumeControls.CreatePrimary` makes one that follows the accent. Not written by the designer. |
| `EffectiveVolume` | `double` | `1` | get | What the audio output is to get: 0 while the control is muted, else the `Volume`. |
| `IsMuted` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the sound is off. The slider stands at 0 while it is, and the `Volume` is remembered. |
| `MuteButton` | `Button` | - | get | The mute button. |
| `ShowPercentage` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the volume is written as a percentage ("60 %") beside the slider, as in players like VLC (off by default). While it is on, the popup of the slider is off, so that the number is not shown twice; the text is 0 % while the control is muted. |
| `Slider` | `TrackBar` | - | get | The slider, for what the control does not offer by itself (the popup, the steps of the keys, its own events). |
| `Target` | `IAudioVolume` | - | get, set | The player (or anything else that makes sound) this control is coupled to; null (the default) is none. On assigning, the control takes over its volume and mute; from then on every change by the user - and every `Volume` or `IsMuted` set from code - is passed on to it (the volume that is remembered and the mute as two things), and the control follows the `VolumeChanged` of the player (also when it is raised on another thread). The control lets go of it when it is disposed. |
| `Volume` | `double` | `1` | get, set | The level the sound has when it is on, from 0 to 1 (1 by default); it is remembered while the control is muted. Setting it from code moves the slider (while it is not muted) without raising `VolumeChanged`; 0 mutes the control and leaves the remembered level as it was, a value above 0 does not turn the sound on. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VolumeChanged` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the user changes what is heard: moves the slider or switches the sound off or on (see `EffectiveVolume`). Not when code sets the volume. |


## AppForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.AppForm` - based on `Form`

A `Form` with ErikwnkWFUI's own title bar (`TitleBar`) instead of the native Windows one: no frame, resizable by its edges, with a system menu (right-click on the title bar, Alt+Space), a drop shadow, and the work area of the screen when it is maximized. This is the base class every ErikwnkWFUI window is built on - make one with `UIStyles.Forms.CreateStandard`, `CreateDialog` or `CreateSettings`, or derive from it and hand `FormOptions` to the constructor, the way `MessageBoxForm` and `UpdateAvailableForm` do. Add your own controls to `ContentPanel`, not directly to the form - the title bar occupies the top of the form's own `Controls`. It opens in the middle of the screen, or over its owner when it has one (`StartPosition` can be changed). `FormTitle` sets the title of the window and of the bar at once; `RememberBoundsKey` makes the window come back where it was.

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateStandard()`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BorderColor` | `Color` | `#0A0A0A` | get, set | The color of the thin edge around the window (a window with the native frame has none): black - the darkest background of the theme, which follows a change of the theme - for every window until a color is set; `Empty` goes back to that. The title bar and the version strip have their own colors (`Colors`). |
| `CloseEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the user can close the window (`CloseEnabled`): with false the close button is greyed out, the entry of the system menu is too, and Alt+F4, the taskbar and Escape do not close it. `Close()` of the program still does (and so does a plain close message, as "End task" sends it). Can be changed while the window is open (a window that has finished its work lets the user close it). The native frame cannot grey out its button: there the click is only without effect. |
| `ContentPanel` | `Panel` | - | get | The panel below the title bar - add your own UI here. |
| `FormIcon` | `Image` | - | get, set | Shorthand for `TitleBar.IconImage` - the small logo shown at the top-left of the title bar, not the OS-level icon (see `WindowIcon` for that). |
| `FormTitle` | `string` | `""` | get, set | The title of the window: the `Text` (taskbar, Alt-Tab) and the title bar show the same text, whichever of the two is set. `TitleBar.Title` changes the bar alone. |
| `RememberBoundsKey` | `string` | `null` | get, set | A name under which the window remembers its position and size between runs (`RememberBoundsKey`): it is saved when the window is closed and restored when it opens, as long as it is still on a screen that is there. Use one name per window of the program. Null (the default) remembers nothing. A fixed-size window remembers only its position. Set it before the window is shown. |
| `TitleBar` | `TitleBarControl` | - | get | The title bar itself - reach through here for anything not already proxied by `FormTitle`/`FormIcon`, e.g. `TitleBar.TitleForeColor`. |
| `VersionLabel` | `Label` | - | get | The reserved bottom-right version strip, or null when `VersionText` wasn't set - reach through here to restyle it (font, color) after construction. |
| `VersionStrip` | `FlowLayoutPanel` | - | get | The reserved bottom-right strip holding `VersionLabel`, or null when it wasn't reserved at all (see `VersionText`). Flows right-to-left, so `VersionStrip.Controls.Add(someControl)` places it directly to the left of the version text - e.g. an `CreateUpdateAvailableButton` button. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `ShowSystemMenu(Point screenPosition)` | Shows the system menu (Restore, Minimize, Maximize, Close) at a place on the screen - what a right-click on the title bar and Alt+Space do. The entries the window cannot do are left out. |


## InfoPopupForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.InfoPopupForm` - based on `PopupFormBase`

A small, borderless popup with extra info next to a control or the mouse, like a tooltip. Its content is blocks of an optional header and an optional text (`SetContent`). Reuse one instance for many show calls: it is moved and refilled instead of being closed and created again. Get one through `UIStyles.InfoPopups`.

Made by `UIStyles.InfoPopups` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the popup: its background is the set's basic color. Left null, the neutral gray (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Gray`); `UIStyles.InfoPopups.CreatePrimary` makes one in the accent color. |
| `Delay` | `PopupDelay` | `Medium` | get, set | How long `ShowAtMouseDelayed` waits before it shows the popup: not at all, 0.2, 0.4 (the default) or 0.8 seconds. |
| `Duration` | `PopupDuration` | `Medium` | get, set | How long the popup stays after it was shown (or moved) before it hides itself: 3, 5 (the default) or 8 seconds. Every show call starts the time again, so a popup that is shown from a MouseMove handler stays while the mouse moves over its control. |
| `FixedSize` | `Size` | - | get, set | The client size the popup keeps whatever its content, with the content centered; for one short value that changes while the popup is shown ("9%" and "100%" must not resize it). Empty (the default) sizes the popup to its content. In pixels. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AttachTo(Control control, string text)` | Shows this popup as the tooltip of `control`: after the `Delay` once the mouse rests on it, at the mouse, once for each time the mouse enters. It goes away when the mouse leaves, on a click or a key press, and when the control is hidden or disposed (which also detaches it). One popup can serve any number of controls, each with its own content. A disabled control gets it too. |
| `AttachTo(Control control, InfoPopupSection[] sections)` | Attaches the blocks; see `AttachTo`. |
| `AttachTo(Control control, Func<InfoPopupSection[]> content)` | Attaches content that is worked out each time the popup is about to show (a value that changes, a text for the current state); see `AttachTo`. |
| `AttachTo(Control control, string header, string text)` | Attaches a header with its text; see `AttachTo`. |
| `CancelPendingShow()` | Cancels a show scheduled by `ShowAtMouseDelayed` that has not happened yet - does not hide the popup if it is already showing. |
| `Detach(Control control)` | Takes the popup off `control` again; a popup that is up for it goes away. |
| `SetContent(InfoPopupSection[] sections)` | Sets what the popup shows: one block per section, each with a header, a text, or both; a section without either is left out. |
| `SetContent(string text)` | Sets a single text, without a header. |
| `SetContent(string header, string text, Color headerColor, Color textColor)` | Sets a header with its text, each in its own color or, left empty, the automatic one. |
| `ShowAtMouse(Control anchor, Point mouseScreenPosition)` | Shows (or moves) the popup near `mouseScreenPosition` - typical use is a MouseMove handler. |
| `ShowAtMouseDelayed(Control anchor, Point mouseScreenPosition, InfoPopupSection[] sections)` | Like `ShowAtMouse` with the given content, but after the `Delay` (at once for `Instant`). For hover tooltips: passing the mouse over several items does not flash a popup for each. Call `CancelPendingShow` on MouseLeave to cancel a show that has not happened yet. |
| `ShowCenteredAbove(Control anchor, int anchorLocalX)` | Shows (or moves) the popup centered horizontally on `anchorLocalX` (a pixel x inside `anchor`) and just above `anchor`; below it if there is no room above. Typical use is a live value readout over a slider thumb. |
| `ShowNextTo(Control anchor)` | Shows (or moves) the popup at the bottom-right of the control `anchor`. |


## InputBoxForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.InputBoxForm` - based on `AppForm`

The themed replacement for the input box of Visual Basic: a small dialog with a prompt, one text box (or a password box) and the buttons OK and Cancel. Make one with `UIStyles.Forms.CreateInputStandard` / `CreateInputPrimary` and show it with `ShowDialog`, or just call `Show`. After `DialogResult.OK` the text is in `Value`. Enter confirms, Escape cancels. Under the prompt there can be a gray `Hint`, and a red `ErrorText` over the box (set it for a wrong entry, or let `Validator` do it). The window has a fixed width and is as high as its texts need, but never higher than the screen (a prompt that is too long is cut at its end). The texts of the buttons and the default title follow the language of the library. Dispose it after `ShowDialog` (`Show` does).

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateInputStandard("")`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowEmpty` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether OK also accepts an empty text. By default it does not: OK does nothing until something is typed. |
| `CancelButtonText` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | get, set | The text of the Cancel button ("Cancel" or "Abbrechen"), or null for the text of the library. |
| `ErrorText` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A message in red over the box, for an entry that was not right (for instance "wrong password" when the program asks again). It is taken away when the user types, and `Validator` sets it. Empty (the default) shows none. |
| `Hint` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A short note in small gray letters under the prompt (what is wanted, an example ...); empty (the default) shows none. |
| `InputTextBox` | `TextBox` | - | get | The box the user types into, for what is not covered here (an input filter ...). |
| `MaxLength` | `int` | `0` | get, set | The most characters the box takes; 0 (the default) is no limit beyond the one of Windows. |
| `OkButtonText` | `string` | `"OK"` | get, set | The text of the OK button: "OK", or null for the text of the library. |
| `Prompt` | `string` | `""` | get, set | The text above the box; the window grows or shrinks to it. |
| `TrimValue` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the spaces at the beginning and the end of the text are cut off: `Value` and the text that `Validator` sees are without them, and a text of spaces only counts as empty. Off by default (a password may begin with a space). |
| `Validator` | `Func<string, string>` | - | get, set | Checks the text when OK is clicked: returns null when it is fine, otherwise the message that is shown in red over the box (the window stays open, the text is selected). Null (the default) accepts every text that is not empty. It is not asked for an empty text unless `AllowEmpty` is set, and it gets the trimmed text when `TrimValue` is set. An exception in it is not caught. |
| `Value` | `string` | `""` | get | The text that was entered, once the dialog was closed with OK (what the user accepted); empty before. |


## MessageBoxForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.MessageBoxForm` - based on `AppForm`

The dialog behind `MessageBox`: a text (it scrolls when it does not fit), an icon in the title bar, and the buttons. Make one with `UIStyles.Forms.CreateMessageStandard` / `CreateMessagePrimary` and show it with `ShowDialog`, or call `MessageBox.Show`. A window that is closed without a button returns the safe result (No for Yes/No, Cancel where there is a Cancel button, Abort for Abort/Retry/Ignore, OK for OK). Ctrl+C copies the text of the box (as the box of Windows does), `Details` adds a text that the user can open under the message, and `MessageBoxDefault` says which button has the focus first.

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateMessageStandard("")`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CheckBoxChecked` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the check box is checked. |
| `CheckBoxText` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A check box under the message ("Do not ask again", "Apply to all"); empty (the default) has none. What the user did with it is `CheckBoxChecked` once the dialog has ended. |
| `Details` | `string` | `""` | get, set | A text under the message that the user opens with the "Details" button (the text of an exception, say); empty (the default) has no button. |
| `DetailsExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the text of `Details` is open (the window is higher then). Closed by default. |
| `PlaySound` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the sound of the icon is played when the window opens (the sounds of Windows for information, warning, error and question). Off by default. |
| `ShowHelpButton` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the box has a help button (a question mark at the left of the buttons) that raises `HelpClicked`. Off by default. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HelpClicked` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the help button is clicked; the dialog stays open. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `GetTextForCopy()` | The text that Ctrl+C copies: the title, the message (and the details), and the names of the buttons, in the form the box of Windows uses. |


## OptionsForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.OptionsForm` - based on `AppForm`

A settings window built around a `PropertyTable`: add your own rows to `PropertyTable`, then call `FitToContent` so the window sizes itself to what was added instead of guessing a size. It is a settings window of `UIStyles.Forms` (the version of the program in a strip at the bottom, `VersionStrip`) with the buttons Save and Cancel, which close it with `DialogResult.OK` and `Cancel`; `ShowButtons` = false leaves them out for a window that applies every change at once. The table is a card in the middle of the window, and it scrolls when the rows are more than the screen has room for (the buttons and the version strip stay). It starts with the ready-made options of the library - theme (a button in the top right corner), accent color, language and always on top (`OptionsPreset`; more are there - start with Windows, reset to defaults - and any selection is added with `AddOption`). They are applied as they are chosen and taken back when the window is closed without Save. Saving also writes the appearance when the program called `UIStyles.RememberAppearance`, and tells the user by a toast (`ShowToasts`). Make one with `UIStyles.Forms.CreateOptionsStandard` or `CreateOptionsPrimary`.

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateOptionsStandard()`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CancelButtonText` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | get, set | The text of the Cancel button, as `SaveButtonText`. |
| `PropertyTable` | `PropertyTable` | - | get | Add your option rows here, then call `FitToContent`. |
| `SaveButtonText` | `string` | `"Save"` | get, set | The text of the Save button: "Save" or "Speichern", by the language of the library (it follows a change of the language while the window is open). A text set here is shown as it is; null goes back to the language of the library. |
| `SelectedAccentColor` | `Color` | `#005A9E` | get | The accent color that is applied now. |
| `SelectedAlwaysOnTop` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the window that owns this one (the main window) is always on top now. |
| `SelectedLanguage` | `UILanguage` | `English` | get | The language of the library that is applied now. |
| `SelectedStartWithWindows` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the program is to start with Windows: what the switch says (written when the user saves), or - without that option - what Windows has. |
| `SelectedTheme` | `UIColorTheme` | - | get | The theme that is applied now (dark or light). |
| `ShowButtons` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the window has the buttons Save and Cancel (the default). Without them it is for settings that are applied at once: the user closes it with the close button of the title bar or Escape, and there is no Enter and Escape handling of buttons. The options of the library that were chosen stay then. |
| `ShowToasts` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the window tells the user by a toast, in the language of the library, that the settings were saved ("Settings saved", over the window that owns this one - none without an owner) and that the defaults were restored (over this window). The default. |
| `StartWithWindowsArguments` | `string` | `null` | get, set | Arguments the program is started with when it starts with Windows (null: none), so it can tell that it was not started by the user - to stay in the tray, say. Used when `StartWithWindows` is saved. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultsRestored` | `EventHandler` | Raised after the button of `ResetToDefaults` has put the options of the library back: reset your own rows here. |
| `SaveClicked` | `EventHandler` | Raised when the save button is clicked and every editor has accepted its value (`Validating` did not cancel), before the dialog closes with DialogResult.OK - read whatever the option controls added to PropertyTable are currently set to here, and the options of the library from `SelectedTheme`, `SelectedAccentColor`, `SelectedLanguage` ... (the start with Windows is written before, the remembered appearance after this event). |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `AddOption(OptionsPreset preset)` | Puts a ready-made option into the table (under the section "General", which is made with the first one): the row, its choice, and what applying it does. The program keeps the result where it keeps its settings: read `SelectedTheme`, `SelectedAccentColor`, `SelectedLanguage` and `SelectedAlwaysOnTop` in `SaveClicked`. An option that is there already is not added twice: its row is returned. The theme has no row (it is a button in the top right corner of the window), so `Theme` returns null. |
| `AddOptions(OptionsPreset[] presets)` | Puts several ready-made options into the table, in this order. |
| `FitToContent(int extraWidth, int extraHeight)` | Sizes the window to exactly fit the rows currently in `PropertyTable` plus the button bar and the version strip - at most as high as the screen allows (then the table scrolls) - call it after the rows are added, instead of guessing a fixed window size. `extraWidth` and `extraHeight` are room (for 96 dpi) added to the width and the height. |


## ProgressForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.ProgressForm` - based on `AppForm`

A small dialog that shows how far a task has come: a text (`Status`) and a progress bar with the percentage on it, or a bar that just moves (`IsIndeterminate`) when the end cannot be told. The task reports with `Report` - from any thread - and the window is also an `IProgress`1`, so it can be handed to a task that wants one. The user cannot close it (the close button is greyed out): the program closes it when the task is done, or ends it with `Succeed` or `Fail` (see below). With `Cancelable` there is a Cancel button (Escape does the same) that asks the task to stop through `CancellationToken`; the window stays until the program closes it. `State` says where it is, and once the task has ended nothing changes any more (late reports are ignored). `ShowTime` adds the time that has passed and the time that is left (an estimate). `Succeed` and `Fail` end the task in the window itself: the bar turns green or red, the text says how it ended, and the user closes the window with the button (now "Close") - so a message can still be read. It is for a task that blocks the program for a while; the reports and the end can come from any thread. Make one with `UIStyles.Forms.CreateProgressStandard` / `CreateProgressPrimary`, or let `Run` do it all.

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateProgressStandard()`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BarColors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the bar while the task runs (its main color, as `UIStyles.ProgressBars.CreateStandard(colors)` uses it): for example `UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Green` for an update, as green as its Update now button. Null (the default) is the color set of the window when it has one, else the accent. Once the task has ended the bar is green (`Succeed`) or red (`Fail`) whatever this is. Set it on the thread of the window. |
| `CancelButtonText` | `string` | `"Cancel"` | get, set | The text of the Cancel button ("Cancel" or "Abbrechen"), or null for the text of the library. When the task has ended (`Succeed`, `Fail`) the button says "Close" whatever this is. |
| `Cancelable` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the window has a Cancel button, which Escape presses too. Cancelling only asks: `IsCancelled` and `CancellationToken` say so, and the task stops and the program closes the window. |
| `CancellationToken` | `CancellationToken` | - | get | Is cancelled when the user asks to stop: give it to the task, which looks at it (or passes it on) and ends. |
| `IsCancelled` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the user has asked to stop. |
| `IsIndeterminate` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the bar just moves, because nobody can tell how long the task takes (the percentage is not shown then). |
| `Percent` | `int` | `0` | get, set | How far the task has come, 0 to 100 (a value outside is cut to it); setting it turns `IsIndeterminate` off. Can be set from any thread. Once the task has ended (`Succeed`, `Fail`) nothing changes any more: late reports are ignored. |
| `ShowPercentage` | `bool` | `true` | get, set | Whether the percentage is written on the bar (the default); a bar that just moves has none. |
| `ShowTime` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether a gray line under the bar says how much time has passed and - when the percentage is known and the task has been running for a moment - how much is left, as an estimate ("0:12 elapsed · about 0:35 left"). Off by default. |
| `State` | `ProgressState` | `Running` | get | Whether the task is still running or has ended with `Succeed` or `Fail`. |
| `Status` | `string` | `""` | get, set | The text above the bar ("Downloading ..."); the window grows or shrinks to it. Can be set from any thread. |

| Event | Handler | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CancelRequested` | `EventHandler` | Raised (on the thread of the window) when the user asks to stop: the Cancel button or Escape. `IsCancelled` is true then. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Fail(string text)` | Ends the task in the window as a failure: the bar stands where it was and is red, the text says what went wrong (so that it can still be read), and the time stops. The button says "Close"; the user can close the window from now on. From any thread. |
| `Report(int percent)` | Reports how far the task has come (`Percent`). From any thread; also what `IProgress`1` asks for. |
| `Report(int percent, string status)` | Reports how far the task has come and what it is doing now (`Percent` and `Status`). From any thread. |
| `Succeed(string text)` | Ends the task in the window: the bar is full and green, the text (when there is one) says how it went, and the time stops. The button now says "Close" and closes the window - the user can close it from now on (the close button, Escape). From any thread. |
