## ToastForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.ToastForm` - based on `PopupFormBase`

A small, rounded, self-dismissing toast: an optional symbol, an optional title and a message. Call the static `ShowToast` (or `UIStyles.Toasts`); a toast cannot be constructed directly. Only one toast shows at a time; a new one closes the one that is up.

Made by `UIStyles.Toasts` (see the end of this file).

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Colors` | `UIColorSet` | - | get, set | The colors of the toast: its background is the set's basic color and the text white or black. Left null, the neutral gray (`UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Gray`); `UIStyles.Toasts.ShowPrimary` makes one in the accent color. |
| `CustomSymbol` | `string` | - | get, set | Any symbol instead of `MessageIcon`, one of `UIStyles.Symbols` (say `UIStyles.Symbols.Copy`) or a character of your own that the symbol font has. Null or empty (the default) uses `MessageIcon`. |
| `Duration` | `PopupDuration` | - | get, set | How long the toast stays before it closes itself. `UntilClicked` has no time: the toast stays until it is clicked (and shows a small cross at its right for that), until a newer toast replaces it or until its window closes. |
| `DurationGrowsWithText` | `bool` | - | get, set | Whether a long text makes the toast stay longer than its `Duration`: the level is the least time, and the time to read the title and the message (about 0.3 seconds a word, 8 seconds at most) is the other. A short message keeps the time of its level. On by default; off gives every toast exactly the time of its level. |
| `MessageIcon` | `ToastIcon` | - | get, set | The symbol at the left of the toast; none by default, then the text has the whole width. |

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `ShowToast(string message, Form owner, UIColorSet colors, PopupTransparency transparency, PopupDuration duration, PopupDelay delay, ToastIcon icon, string symbol, ToastPosition position, bool durationGrowsWithText)` | Shows a toast in `owner`, at `position`, closing itself after `duration`. If `owner` is not in front, the toast waits until it is. |
| `ShowToast(InfoPopupSection content, Form owner, UIColorSet colors, PopupTransparency transparency, PopupDuration duration, PopupDelay delay, ToastIcon icon, string symbol, ToastPosition position, bool durationGrowsWithText)` | Like the call with a message, but with a title above the message and, if wanted, own colors for each (`HeaderColor` for the title, `TextColor` for the message). A part left empty is not shown; with neither there is no toast. |


## UpdateAvailableForm

`ErikwnkWFUI.Forms.UpdateAvailableForm` - based on `AppForm`

The dialog behind `UpdatePrompt.ShowUpdateAvailableAsync` - prefer calling that over constructing this directly: it shows this dialog and then, when the user chose to update, the progress of the download. After `ShowDialog``UpdateChosen` says whether "Update now" was clicked and `SkipChosen` whether "Skip this version" was. `ReleaseNotes` adds a "What's new" button that opens the text of the release under the versions.

Made by `UIStyles.Forms` (see the end of this file).

The defaults below are those of `UIStyles.Forms.CreateUpdateAvailableStandard("", "")`: the type has no constructor without parameters.

| Property | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowSkip` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the window has a "Skip this version" button (the program then does not ask again for this version). Off by default. |
| `NotesExpanded` | `bool` | `false` | get, set | Whether the text of `ReleaseNotes` is open (the window is higher then). Closed by default. |
| `ReleaseNotes` | `string` | `""` | get, set | The text of the release ("What's new"): with it the window has a "What's new" button that opens the text under the versions. Empty (the default) has no button. Plain text; the Markdown of a GitHub release is shown as it is written. |
| `SkipChosen` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the user clicked "Skip this version" (the dialog is closed with `DialogResult.Ignore` then). The button is there only with `AllowSkip`. |
| `UpdateChosen` | `bool` | `false` | get | Whether the user clicked "Update now" (the dialog is closed with `DialogResult.Yes` then); false for Later, Skip and for closing it. |


## Other public types

Helpers, static entry points and the like that are not controls. The enumerations follow with their values.

| Type | Kind | Namespace | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AppCurrencyFormatter` | static class | ErikwnkWFUI | Formats amounts for a chosen currency - deliberately independent of AppLanguage/AppLocalization. Someone reading German text doesn't necessarily want US number formatting just because they picked Dollar, and vice versa, so this only controls the currency symbol and its own number format, not the rest of the UI. |
| `UIStyles` | static class | ErikwnkWFUI | The single entry point for ErikwnkWFUI's control factories and styling - start here rather than the individual classes under `Factories`/`Styles` (most of which are internal). Each nested class below (`UIStyles.Buttons`, `UIStyles.Labels`, ...) mirrors one control type with a set of `Create*` factory methods that return a pre-themed, ready-to-add WinForms control. See `UIStyles.Colors` for how to customize the color scheme (accent color and/or full light/dark theme) and `UIStyles.Language`/`UIStyles.SetLanguage` for switching the language of built-in dialog text. |
| `LabelScroll` | class | Controls | How the text of a `ScrollingLabel` moves when it is too long for the label, all in one value to hand to `UIStyles.Labels` (or to `Scroll`): `LabelScroll.Endless()`, `LabelScroll.BackAndForth(LabelScrollSpeed.Fast)`. It cannot be changed; one value can serve any number of labels. |
| `PropertyColumn` | class | Controls | Pairs a `Control` (or a null placeholder) with a `TableLayoutPanel` column width, for `PropertyTable`'s multi-column row overloads. Build one with `Auto`, `Absolute`, or `Percent` rather than constructing it directly. |
| `PropertyRow` | class | Controls | A row (or section header) of a `PropertyTable`, as `AddRow` and `AddSection` return it: it can be hidden or disabled later, for an option that depends on another one. After `ClearRows` the row is gone and the handle does nothing any more. |
| `RadioGroup` | class | Controls | One choice among several radio buttons that do not have to share a parent: the standard grouping works only for buttons in the same container, which is awkward in a table layout or when a choice is spread over several panels. Put the buttons into a group; selecting one clears the others, and `SelectionChanged` tells the new choice once. |
| `TabAddingEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabAdding`. |
| `TabClosingEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabClosing`. |
| `TabRenameStartingEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabRenameStarting`. |
| `TabRenamedEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabRenamed`. |
| `TabRenamingEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabRenaming`. |
| `TabRightClickEventArgs` | class | Controls | Data for `TabRightClick`. |
| `UIColumn` (obsolete) | class | Controls | The old name of `PropertyColumn`: `UIColumn.Percent(...)`, `Absolute` and `Auto` still work (and give a `PropertyColumn`); code that declares a variable of the type `UIColumn` has to use `PropertyColumn`. It is removed once the projects that use it have been changed. |
| `AppUpdater` | class | Forms | Self-contained "check for update" flow for apps hosting their releases on GitHub. Provides all the UI itself (prompt, progress, failure message) and only needs the repo coordinates and a couple of HttpClients to talk to ErikwnkCore.Updater - the consuming app never touches that library directly. |
| `FormOptions` | class | Forms | Everything that can be set for an `AppForm`. Start from one of the factory methods and change single properties from there, rather than writing `new FormOptions { ... }`: the presets keep related properties together (a dialog has no maximize button AND cannot be maximized by dragging, and closes with Escape). `CreateStandard` is a resizable window, `CreateDialog` a fixed-size one with only the close button, `CreateSettings` a dialog with the version of the program; the `CreatePrimary...` ones have the frame in the accent. `UIStyles.Forms` makes the window itself from such options. |
| `FormSizeOption` | struct | Forms | The size of a window or dialog: one of the three `FormSize` values or an own `Size`, one parameter for both - `size: FormSize.Small` or `size: new Size(500, 300)` (both convert by themselves). An own size is for 96 dpi like the ready-made ones. For a dialog whose height follows its content (input box, progress dialog, options window) the width is the one that is given, and the height is the least height: the content decides when it needs more. |
| `InfoPopupSection` | class | Forms | One block of content for `InfoPopupForm`: a header, a text, or both. A part left null or empty is not shown. |
| `InputBox` | static class | Forms | The themed replacement for the input box of Visual Basic - call `Show`. It is shown as a dialog and returns what the user typed. |
| `MessageBox` | static class | Forms | ErikwnkWFUI's themed replacement for `MessageBox` - call `Show`. |
| `PopupFormBase` | abstract class | Forms | What `InfoPopupForm` and `ToastForm` have in common: a borderless window that is never in the taskbar, never takes the activation, has smoothly rounded corners and a thin line around it (and, as Windows 11 would give a window it rounds itself, no shadow), is see-through by a `PopupTransparency` and moves with the window it belongs to. |
| `ProgressBox` | static class | Forms | Shows a progress dialog while a task runs - call `Run`. It is shown as a dialog and closes by itself when the task is done. |
| `StyledFormOptions` (obsolete) | class | Forms | The old name of `FormOptions`: its factory methods still work (and give a `FormOptions`); code that declares a variable of the type `StyledFormOptions` has to use `FormOptions`. |
| `Toaster` | class | Forms | The settings of a toast kept as properties, to show toasts with them again and again (like `InfoPopupForm` keeps its settings): created with `UIStyles.Toasts.CreateStandard` or `CreatePrimary`, changed at any time, used by every toast it shows from then on. A toast that is already up is not changed. It holds no window of its own, so it needs no disposing; the toasts it shows are `ToastForm`s with all their rules (one at a time, waiting for the window). |
| `UpdatePrompt` | static class | Forms | The windows of an update: the question "a new version is available" and, after "Update now", the progress of the download. Both are modal and have to be shown from the thread of the application's windows (the UI thread). |
| `BorderlessResizeHandler` | class | Helpers | Restores edge/corner resize cursors and dragging for a borderless (`None`) form, which loses that automatically along with its native frame. `AppForm` already wires this up for you when its Borderless/Resizable options are both true - construct one directly only if you're building a borderless window from scratch instead of deriving from AppForm. |
| `OutsideClickFilter` | class | Helpers | Watches the whole application for a mouse button going down and calls back when `isOutside` says it landed somewhere that counts as "elsewhere" for the owner. Never swallows the click. Start it when the owner needs it, stop it (or dispose it) when done. |
| `TextDragDropHelper` | static class | Helpers | Helper for adding drag and drop support to controls. TextDragDropHelper.EnableTextDragDrop( txtPath, text => txtPath.Text = text); |
| `ToolTipActivationFix` | static class | Helpers | Works around a WinForms/Windows quirk where a `ToolTip` can silently stop popping up once its owning top-level window has lost and regained focus (e.g. Alt-Tab) - the native tooltip control's internal activation state gets left off and normal mouse hover no longer reactivates it. Toggling `Active` off then on again resets that state; this hooks it automatically to the owning `Form`'s `Activated` event, following the control through reparenting. |
| `WindowsAutoStart` | static class | Helpers | Whether the program starts when the user signs in to Windows: the entry of the program in the "Run" key of the user (`HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`), named like the program. It needs no rights of an administrator and is the same list Windows shows in Task Manager, "Startup apps". The state lives in Windows, not in the program's own settings. A program that the user has switched off in Task Manager ("Startup apps") is not started with Windows, whatever the Run key says: `IsEnabled` says so, and `Set` switches it on again. |
| `UIAccentColors` | static class | Styles | A curated palette of base colors for `SetAccent`, picked at roughly the same brightness/saturation as `Blue` (the default) so every choice produces a comparably good set of derived light/dark shades. Not exhaustive - SetAccent takes any Color, this is just a ready-made "pick one" set for a color-picker UI. |
| `UIAppearance` | class | Styles | What the user chose to make the library look like: theme, accent color and language - the part of the settings that belongs to the library. Only plain values (an enum, a text, an enum), so it can be a member of the program's own settings class and be written with whatever the program writes its settings with; or it is kept in a file of its own with `Save` and `Load`. `Capture` reads what is applied now, `Apply` applies it. |
| `UIButtonPreset` | class | Styles | A ready-made design for a symbol button: which symbol it carries and in which colors. Pass one to `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateSymbol` and the button gets both. The library's own are in `UIStyles.Buttons.Presets` (Add, Delete, Save ...); your own are made with the constructor, or from one of those with `WithSymbol` / `WithColors`, and can be defined once and used everywhere. |
| `UIColorSet` | class | Styles | Every color a control needs to show one colored look in all of its states: the fill at rest, hovered, pressed and disabled, and the text color that reads best on each of them. Get one from the ready-made `UIStyles.Colors.Sets` (Orange, Teal, Purple ...) or build one from any color with `UIStyles.Colors.CreateSet`; a control that accepts a set then needs nothing else. |
| `UIColorTheme` | class | Styles | The set of base surface colors (backgrounds, text, borders, hover/active tints) that make up a theme - everything except the accent color, which is set independently via `SetAccent` so any accent can be combined with either theme. Property names describe each color's role (e.g. "the default control surface"), not its literal shade - in `Light`, "BackgroundLighter" still means "the most raised/active surface", even though it holds a darker RGB value than "BackgroundMedium" there (you can't go lighter than white, so the light theme's hover/press feedback works by adding a bit of gray instead). Defaults to today's dark values, so creating one and overriding just a few properties still yields a complete, usable theme. |
| `UIColors` | static class | Styles | The colors of the library: the base colors of the theme (backgrounds, text, borders), the shades of the accent and the fixed green, yellow and red families. A control reads them when it paints and follows `ApplyTheme` and `SetAccent` by itself (see `ThemeChanged`). The values are static and not locked: change the theme and the accent from the UI thread. |
| `UIFonts` | static class | Styles | The fonts used across ErikwnkWFUI's controls - fixed, not part of the theme system. |
| `UIIcons` | static class | Styles | The icons that ship with the library (a web page, a folder, a document, a program), as images made from the embedded resources, and two helpers for your own: `Resize` and `LoadEmbedded`. |
| `UIThemes` | static class | Styles | Ready-to-use base themes for `ApplyTheme`. Dark matches ErikwnkWFUI's original, always-has-been-the-default palette exactly (applying it is a no-op unless something else already changed the theme). Light is a from-scratch light palette, not a per-channel inversion of Dark - see the note on `UIColorTheme` about why the same role can hold a lighter or darker RGB value depending on which theme is active. |

| Enumeration | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AppCurrency` | `Euro`, `Dollar` | The currencies `AppCurrencyFormatter` writes amounts in. |
| `CellBorderLines` | `All`, `OuterOnly`, `InnerOnly` | Which lines of a table with `CellBorderStyle.Single` are shown (`CellBorderLines`). |
| `CopyConfirmationStyle` | `Toast`, `ToolTip`, `None` | How `ListView` confirms a Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Shift+C copy. |
| `LabelScrollDirection` | `Left`, `Right` | Which way the text of a `ScrollingLabel` moves in the endless mode. |
| `LabelScrollMode` | `None`, `BackAndForth`, `Endless` | Whether and how the text of a `ScrollingLabel` moves when it is too long for the label. |
| `LabelScrollPause` | `Short`, `Medium`, `Long` | How long the text of a `ScrollingLabel` rests at its start and at its end while it scrolls: 1, 2.2 or 4 seconds. |
| `LabelScrollSeparator` | `Dot`, `Bar`, `Diamond`, `None` | The sign between the end of the text and its next appearance in the endless mode. |
| `LabelScrollSpeed` | `Slow`, `Medium`, `Fast` | How fast the text of a `ScrollingLabel` moves while it scrolls: 25, 45 or 90 pixels per second. |
| `SlimProgressBarTextPosition` | `Above`, `Below`, `Left`, `Right` | Where the text of a `SlimProgressBar` is placed in relation to the bar. |
| `SpinnerSpeed` | `Slow`, `Medium`, `Fast` | How fast the arc of a `Spinner` turns: a turn in about 2, 1.2 or 0.7 seconds. |
| `SpinnerTextPosition` | `Right`, `Left`, `Above`, `Below` | Where the text of a `Spinner` is placed in relation to the ring. |
| `FormSize` | `Small`, `Medium`, `Large` | The three sizes every window and dialog of the library can have. What a size means depends on the kind of window: a normal window is larger than a dialog, a progress dialog is wider than an input box is high, and so on (see `FormSizeOption`); the sizes are given for 96 dpi and scaled to the screen. |
| `MessageBoxButtons` | `OK`, `OKCancel`, `YesNo`, `YesNoCancel`, `RetryCancel`, `AbortRetryIgnore` | Which buttons a `MessageBox` shows. |
| `MessageBoxDefault` | `Safe`, `Button1`, `Button2`, `Button3` | Which button of a `MessageBox` has the focus first (and answers Enter). |
| `MessageBoxIcon` | `None`, `Info`, `Warning`, `Error`, `Question`, `Success` | Which icon a `MessageBox` shows in its title bar. |
| `MessageBoxSize` (obsolete) | `Small`, `Medium`, `Large` | Overall size preset for a `MessageBox`. Use `FormSize`, the one size setting of all the windows. |
| `OptionsPreset` | `Theme`, `AccentColor`, `Language`, `AlwaysOnTop`, `StartWithWindows`, `ResetToDefaults` | A ready-made option of the library for an `OptionsForm`: `AddOption(OptionsPreset.Language)` puts the row with its choice into the table, and the window applies it as it is chosen. What the user chose stays when the window is closed with Save and is taken back when it is closed without (Cancel, Escape, the close button). |
| `PopupDelay` | `Instant`, `Short`, `Medium`, `Long` | How long a popup waits before it shows: a hover `InfoPopupForm` (default medium, so passing the mouse over items shows nothing) or a `ToastForm` (default instant). |
| `PopupDuration` | `Short`, `Medium`, `Long`, `UntilClicked` | How long a popup stays before it closes itself: a `ToastForm` 1.5, 2.5 or 4 seconds, an `InfoPopupForm` 3, 5 or 8 seconds (it is read, not just seen). A toast whose text is long stays longer (see `DurationGrowsWithText`), and `UntilClicked` keeps it until it is clicked. |
| `PopupTransparency` | `Opaque`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | How see-through a popup (`InfoPopupForm`, `ToastForm`) is. |
| `ProgressOutcome` | `Completed`, `Cancelled` | How `Run` ended. |
| `ProgressState` | `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed` | Where a `ProgressForm` is: still working, or finished with `Succeed` or `Fail`. |
| `StyledFormType` (obsolete) | `Standard`, `Dialog`, `Settings` | Only `Settings` did something (the version strip); `CreateSettings` does it now. |
| `ToastIcon` | `None`, `Success`, `Info`, `Warning`, `Error` | The symbol at the left of a `ToastForm`: it tells at a glance what kind of message it is. |
| `ToastPosition` | `BelowCenter`, `Center`, `AboveCenter`, `TopCenter`, `BottomCenter`, `TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomLeft`, `BottomRight` | Where a `ToastForm` is shown inside the window it belongs to. The positions at an edge or in a corner keep a fixed distance from the edge, they never touch it. |
| `UpdateOutcome` | `Declined`, `Applied`, `Failed`, `Skipped`, `Cancelled` | How an `UpdatePrompt.ShowUpdateAvailableAsync` dialog ended. |
| `UILanguage` | `English`, `German` | The language of the built-in dialogs and tooltips - see `UIStyles.Language`. |
| `UIThemeKind` | `Dark`, `Light` | The two ready-made themes by name, so they can be kept in a settings file. |

## UIStyles factory classes

### UIStyles.Buttons

Flat, themed `Button`s with a caption: `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateStandard` (neutral), `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary` (accent color), `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateGreen` (confirm) and `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateRed` (delete). The disabled, hover and pressed looks are built in. A button that carries a symbol instead of a caption always comes from `CreateSymbol`, in one of two ways: with a ready-made `UIStyles.Buttons.Presets` (`CreateSymbol(Presets.Add, "Add")`), or by choosing the symbol and the colors yourself (`CreateSymbol(Symbols.Folder, "Choose folder", size, Colors.Sets.Yellow)`).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateGreen(string text = "", string tooltip = "", Size? size = null, bool isIcon = false)` | A green button, for confirming. |
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "", string tooltip = "", Size? size = null, bool isIcon = false)` | The main button of a screen, in the current accent color. |
| `CreateRed(string text = "", string tooltip = "", Size? size = null, bool isIcon = false)` | A red button, for deleting or other destructive actions. |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", string tooltip = "", Size? size = null, bool isIcon = false, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The neutral button. |
| `CreateSymbol(UIButtonPreset preset, string tooltip = "", Size? size = null)` | Makes a symbol button from a ready-made design - the simplest way. The `preset` already says which symbol the button carries and in which colors; you only add what the button is for (the tooltip) and, if the standard 30 x 30 is not what you want, its size. |
| `CreateSymbol(string symbol, string tooltip = "", Size? size = null, UIColorSet colors = null)` | Makes a symbol button when you want to choose the symbol and the colors yourself: any symbol from `UIStyles.Symbols` (or a symbol of your own), in the neutral look or in the colors of a color set. |
| `CreateThemeToggle(Size? size = null, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The old name of `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateThemeToggleStandard`; it is removed once the projects that use it have been changed. |
| `CreateThemeTogglePrimary(Size? size = null)` | The button that switches the theme (see `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateThemeToggleStandard`) in the accent color (it follows a change of the accent). |
| `CreateThemeToggleStandard(Size? size = null, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A button that switches the theme, and does all of it by itself: it shows the symbol of the theme a click leads to (the sun for the light one, the moon for the dark one), switches the theme with `UIColors.ApplyTheme` when it is clicked, and shows the new state - also when the theme is changed by anything else (the options window, your own code). Its tooltip and its name for the screen reader say what a click does, in the language of the library, and follow a change of it. It takes no focus, like a button of a tool bar. Add a handler to `Click` (it runs after the theme has been switched) to keep the choice, say `UIAppearance.Capture().Save(path)`. |
| `UpdateTooltip(Button button, string tooltip)` | Changes the tooltip text of a button made by this class, for example after a language switch. A button created without a tooltip gets one with the first text that is not empty. |

### UIStyles.CheckBoxes

Themed `CheckBox`es, drawn by the library: `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreateStandard` (neutral gray when checked) and `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimary` (the accent color), each also as a label-less `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreateStandardCompact` / `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimaryCompact` for table cells. A color set can be given to any of the standard ones. Hover, pressed, keyboard focus, disabled and the undetermined third state (`ThreeState`) are built in.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "", bool isChecked = true)` | Like `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreateStandard` but with the box filled in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreatePrimaryCompact(bool isChecked = true)` | Like `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreateStandardCompact` but with the box filled in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - the compact counterpart to `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", bool isChecked = true, UIColorSet colors = null)` |  |
| `CreateStandardCompact(bool isChecked = true, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A box without a label, 25 x 25 (for table cells and the like). |

### UIStyles.Colors

Read-only access to every color used across ErikwnkWFUI's controls, plus `UIStyles.Colors.SetAccent`/`UIStyles.Colors.ApplyTheme` to customize them. Defaults to a dark gray theme with a blue accent; nothing here needs to be set unless you want to change that.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `ApplyTheme(UIColorTheme theme)` | Switches the base theme (backgrounds/text/borders), e.g. UIThemes.Light to move off the dark default. May be called at any time: the controls that exist follow the change by themselves (a color set on a control by hand stays). Combine freely with SetAccent - the two are independent (e.g. a light theme with a purple accent). |
| `CreateSet(Color color)` | A color set made from any color: the color is what a control shows while hovered, the fill at rest is a darker shade and pressed a lighter one (a light color such as yellow keeps its look at rest and gets darker instead). Text and disabled colors are worked out so the text stays readable on every fill. Pass the result to a control that takes a `UIColorSet`. |
| `CreateSet(Color basic, Color hover, Color pressed)` | A color set from the three fills you want (at rest, hovered, pressed); the text and disabled colors are worked out from them. |
| `CreateSet(Color basic, Color hover, Color pressed, Color text)` | Like `UIStyles.Colors.CreateSet`, but the text has the one color you give in every state (muted when disabled) instead of the best one for each fill - for a look whose text color is fixed. |
| `SetAccent(Color accent)` | Replaces the blue accent used throughout every built-in control (buttons, toggle switches, selection highlights, ...) with shades computed from a single color. May be called at any time: the controls that exist follow the change by themselves (see `UIStyles.Colors.ThemeChanged`). |

### UIStyles.ComboBoxes

A themed `ComboBox`: the closed box, the rows and the frame of the open list follow the theme (the scroll bars of the list are the system's dark ones in a dark theme).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(ComboBoxStyle comboBoxStyle = DropDownList)` | Like `UIStyles.ComboBoxes.CreateStandard` but with the selected row in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(ComboBoxStyle comboBoxStyle = DropDownList, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A themed combo box; the selected (or hovered) row of the list is the neutral gray. |
| `ReplaceItems(ComboBox comboBox, IEnumerable<object> items, bool keepSelection = true)` | Clears the items of `comboBox` and fills it from `items` - for example because a language switch changed the texts - and selects again what was selected before, by its POSITION in the list (so the same choices in the same order are assumed, only relabeled). `SelectedIndexChanged` can be raised once by the clearing and once by the selecting. |

### UIStyles.ContextMenuStrips

A `ContextMenuStrip` themed to match the rest of ErikwnkWFUI instead of the plain OS-default popup menu - functionally identical to the native control.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | Like `UIStyles.ContextMenuStrips.CreateStandard` but with the highlight in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A themed context menu; the hovered item is the neutral gray. |

### UIStyles.DataGridViews

A themed `DataGridView` for data bound via `DataSource` - the control to reach for when rows come from a bound source rather than being added by hand.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(object dataSource = null)` | Like `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreateStandard` but framed in the current accent color instead of the fixed neutral border - mirrors `UIStyles.ListViews.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateReadOnlyPrimary(object dataSource = null)` | Like `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreateReadOnlyStandard` but framed in the current accent color instead of the fixed neutral border - the read-only counterpart to `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateReadOnlyStandard(object dataSource = null, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The display-only variant - column-header sorting, but no editing. Use `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreateStandard` instead for a grid that needs to be editable. |
| `CreateStandard(object dataSource = null, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The editable variant - row adding/deleting, an optional delete-row column, clipboard cut/copy/paste, and a right-click context menu. Use `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreateReadOnlyStandard` instead for a grid that only ever shows data. |

### UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels

A `FlowLayoutPanel` with no padding/margin, in the elevated background of the theme or transparent. It differs from the standard one in two settings: it is as big as its content (`AutoSize`; the transparent one is never smaller than a standard panel, 200 x 100, as it has always been) and does not wrap (`WrapContents` is off); both can be set again. `FlowDirection` and `AutoScroll` (scroll bars in the style of the theme) work as in the standard control. There is no frame; set `BorderStyle = FixedSingle` (a thin frame in the color of the theme) and cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.FlowLayoutPanel` for `BorderColor` (another color). Right-to-left layouts are not supported.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | A flow layout panel in a very dark shade of the accent (`UIColors.PrimaryDarkDark`, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary`), otherwise like `UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels.CreateStandard`. Follows a change of the theme and of the accent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A flow layout panel in the elevated background of the theme (`UIColors.BackgroundMediumElevated`, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreateElevated`) that is as big as its content and does not wrap, without margin and padding. Follows a change of the theme. For a row of controls on a surface, use `UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels.CreateTransparent`. |
| `CreateTransparent()` | A flow layout panel without a background of its own (what lies behind it shows through), otherwise like `UIStyles.FlowLayoutPanels.CreateStandard`. |

### UIStyles.Fonts

The fonts used across ErikwnkWFUI's controls.

(no methods)

### UIStyles.Forms

Windows with the title bar of the library, ready to use: `UIStyles.Forms.CreateStandard("My app")`, then put the content into its `ContentPanel`. A window of your own derives from `AppForm` and takes the same options (`FormOptions`) in its constructor. Standard windows can be resized, minimized and maximized; a dialog has only the close button and a fixed size; a settings window is a dialog with the version of the program in a strip at the bottom (a darker gray than the content, in every window). The title bar is the darkest background of the theme, in the basic color of a color set (`colors:`) or, with `CreatePrimary...`, in a very dark shade of the accent that follows a change of the accent; its three buttons have the colors of the set (the symbols look as in every window). The thin edge around the window is black in all of them (`AppForm.BorderColor` changes it). A window that can be resized has a least size (`FormOptions.MinimumSize`).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateDialogPrimary(string title = "", ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleCenter, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A fixed-size dialog with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateDialogStandard(string title = "", UIColorSet colors = null, ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleCenter, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A fixed-size dialog: only the close button, and it cannot be maximized by dragging. |
| `CreateInputPrimary(string prompt, string title = null, string text = "", bool password = false, string placeholder = "", FormSizeOption? size = null)` | An input box with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateInputStandard(string prompt, string title = null, string text = "", bool password = false, UIColorSet colors = null, string placeholder = "", FormSizeOption? size = null)` | An input box (`InputBoxForm`): a small dialog with a prompt, one text box and OK / Cancel. Show it with `ShowDialog`; after OK the text is in `Value`. `Show` does all of it in one call. |
| `CreateMessagePrimary(string message, string title = null, MessageBoxButtons buttons = OK, MessageBoxIcon icon = Info, FormSizeOption? size = null, string details = null, MessageBoxDefault defaultButton = Safe, String[] buttonTexts = null, bool playSound = false)` | A message box with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateMessageStandard(string message, string title = null, MessageBoxButtons buttons = OK, MessageBoxIcon icon = Info, UIColorSet colors = null, FormSizeOption? size = null, string details = null, MessageBoxDefault defaultButton = Safe, String[] buttonTexts = null, bool playSound = false)` | A message box (`MessageBoxForm`): a dialog with a text, an icon in the title bar and buttons. Show it with `ShowDialog` and read `DialogResult`; `MessageBox.Show` does all of it in one call. |
| `CreateOptionsPrimary(string title = null, OptionsPreset[] presets = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | An options window with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateOptionsStandard(string title = null, UIColorSet colors = null, OptionsPreset[] presets = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A settings window around a property table, with the buttons Save and Cancel and the version of the program at the bottom (`OptionsForm`): it starts with the ready-made options of the library (theme, accent color, language, always on top), then add rows to its `PropertyTable` and call `FitToContent()`. |
| `CreatePrimary(string title = "", ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleCenter, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A resizable window with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateProgressPrimary(string status = "", string title = null, bool cancelable = false, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A progress dialog with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateProgressStandard(string status = "", string title = null, bool cancelable = false, UIColorSet colors = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A progress dialog (`ProgressForm`): a text and a progress bar, which the task fills with `Report` (from any thread). The user cannot close it; the program does, when the task is done. `Run` does all of it in one call. |
| `CreateSettingsPrimary(string title = "", ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleLeft, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A settings window with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateSettingsStandard(string title = "", UIColorSet colors = null, ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleLeft, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A dialog like `UIStyles.Forms.CreateDialogStandard` with the version of the program (the entry assembly) in a strip at the bottom. |
| `CreateStandard(string title = "", UIColorSet colors = null, ContentAlignment titleTextAlign = MiddleCenter, Image icon = null, Icon windowIcon = null, FormSizeOption? size = null)` | A resizable window with minimize, maximize and close. |
| `CreateUpdateAvailablePrimary(string currentVersion, string latestVersion, string title = null, FormSizeOption? size = null, string releaseNotes = null, bool allowSkip = false)` | The window that tells the user a new version is there, with the title bar in a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateUpdateAvailableStandard(string currentVersion, string latestVersion, string title = null, UIColorSet colors = null, FormSizeOption? size = null, string releaseNotes = null, bool allowSkip = false)` | The window that tells the user a new version is there (`UpdateAvailableForm`): the two versions and the buttons "Later" and "Update now". Show it with `ShowDialog`; `UpdateChosen` says whether "Update now" was clicked. `UpdatePrompt.ShowUpdateAvailableAsync` does all of it, with the download that follows. |

### UIStyles.GroupBoxes

Themed `GroupBox`es, drawn by the library: a thin rounded frame with the title in a gap of its upper edge. `UIStyles.GroupBoxes.CreateStandard` has the quiet line of the theme (or the color of a set), `UIStyles.GroupBoxes.CreatePrimary` a frame in the current accent. The surface is the one of the parent; the children are added as to any group box.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "")` | Like `UIStyles.GroupBoxes.CreateStandard` but with the frame in the current accent - mirrors `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", UIColorSet colors = null)` |  |

### UIStyles.Icons

ErikwnkWFUI's own bundled icons (Web/Folder/Document/Application), plus `UIStyles.Icons.LoadEmbedded` for loading your own app's icon from its embedded resources the same way - see ErikwnkWFUI/README.md for why that's preferable to a loose file.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `LoadEmbedded(Assembly assembly, string resourceName)` | An image from an embedded resource of an assembly, a copy that belongs to the caller. See `LoadEmbedded` for the exceptions. |

### UIStyles.InfoPopups

A small, borderless popup with extra info next to a control or the mouse: blocks of an optional header and an optional text. Set its content, then show it. Reuse one popup for many show calls.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(Size? fixedSize = null, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Medium)` | Like `UIStyles.InfoPopups.CreateStandard` but in the current accent color instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null, Size? fixedSize = null, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Medium)` | A popup in the neutral gray. |

### UIStyles.Labels

Themed `Label`s: `UIStyles.Labels.CreateStandard` (body text, gray) and `UIStyles.Labels.CreatePrimary` (in the accent color), plus `UIStyles.Labels.CreateTitle` (bold, larger) and `UIStyles.Labels.CreateMuted` (de-emphasized). Each can move its text when it is too long for the label (`scroll`, see `LabelScroll`).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateMuted(string text = "", UIColorSet colors = null, LabelScroll scroll = null)` | De-emphasized text: smaller and dimmer than the standard one. With a color set the text takes its main color, dimmed toward the page behind it, so it stays quiet. |
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "", LabelScroll scroll = null)` | Like `UIStyles.Labels.CreateStandard` but in the current accent color instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", UIColorSet colors = null, LabelScroll scroll = null)` | Body text in the neutral gray. |
| `CreateTitle(string text = "", UIColorSet colors = null, LabelScroll scroll = null)` | A heading: bold and larger, centered, on the background it sits on (transparent). |

### UIStyles.ListBoxes

A themed, owner-drawn, optionally drag-reorderable `ListBox` - a heavier alternative to the native ListBox with icons, custom item colors, and enumeration support. See `UIStyles.TitledListBoxes` for one with a title above it.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(string displayMember = null, bool allowReorder = false, bool showEnumeration = false)` | Like `UIStyles.ListBoxes.CreateStandard` but with the selection and the drop line in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.ListViews.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string displayMember = null, bool allowReorder = false, bool showEnumeration = false, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The list box in neutral gray. |

### UIStyles.ListViews

A dark-themed, multi-column `ListView` (Details view) with spreadsheet-style cell-range selection, hand-rolled column reordering/resizing, and Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Shift+C copy - see the class itself for the full behavior.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | Like `UIStyles.ListViews.CreateStandard`, but the border, the selection, the column drag line and the selection of the context menu follow the accent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | The themed list view in neutral gray. |

### UIStyles.MultiPanels

Panels with several pages, of which one is shown at a time, like the pages of a book. A header on top holds the number of the page (`ShowPageCount`, like "3/12", off by default), the title of the page (`TitleAlignment`: left, the default, center or right) and two small arrows to the previous and the next page. Make one, add the pages with `AddPage(title)` and put the controls of each page on the page that comes back; `SelectedIndex`, `Next()`, `Previous()` and `SelectedIndexChanged` switch and follow the pages. The flat ones and the cards are the same control; the cards are rounded with a thin line (see `UIStyles.Panels.CreateCardStandard`). Follow a change of the theme and of the accent.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateCardPrimary()` | A multi panel as a card in the very dark shade of the accent, with a line one step lighter. Does not dock. |
| `CreateCardStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A multi panel as a card: the elevated background, smoothly rounded corners and a thin line; with a color set in its basic color and the hover color of the set as the line. Does not dock. |
| `CreatePrimary()` | A flat multi panel in a very dark shade of the accent, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary`. Fills its parent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A flat multi panel in the medium background of the theme, or with a color set in its basic color. Fills its parent. |

### UIStyles.NumericUpDowns

A themed `NumericUpDown`: `UIStyles.NumericUpDowns.CreateStandard` (neutral gray arrow fields, or those of a color set) and `UIStyles.NumericUpDowns.CreatePrimary` (in the accent). The field takes the background of the theme (the same as the text box and the combo box, dimmed when disabled) and a frame; the two arrow fields are drawn by the library. The control also has a `Prefix` and a `Suffix` for a unit in the field: cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.NumericUpDown`.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(decimal minimum = 0, decimal maximum = 100, decimal increment = 1, decimal value = 0)` | Like `UIStyles.NumericUpDowns.CreateStandard` but with the arrow fields in the current accent. |
| `CreateStandard(decimal minimum = 0, decimal maximum = 100, decimal increment = 1, decimal value = 0, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A themed numeric up/down with neutral gray arrow fields, or with those of a color set. |

### UIStyles.Panels

Plain `Panel`s pre-filled with one of the theme's background shades - handy as containers/cards. They are the standard panel in every other way (`AutoScroll`, `AutoSize`, `BackgroundImage`, `Padding` and so on): the scroll bars take the style of the theme, a color set by hand stays when the theme changes. They have no frame; set `BorderStyle = FixedSingle` (a thin frame in the color of the theme) and cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.Panel` for `BorderColor` (another color). Right-to-left layouts are not supported.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateCardPrimary()` | The card (see `UIStyles.Panels.CreateCardStandard`) in the very dark shade of the accent of `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary`, with a line one step lighter (`UIColors.PrimaryDark`). Follows a change of the theme and of the accent. |
| `CreateCardStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A card: a panel in the elevated background with smoothly rounded corners and a thin line around it, for a group of controls on a page; it shows what is behind it in its corners. With a color set it is in the basic color of the set and its line has the hover color of the set. It does not dock. Cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.CardPanel` for `CornerRadius`, `BorderStyle` (None or FixedSingle) and `BorderColor`; the card keeps the controls inside away from the corners with a padding of its own. |
| `CreateDark()` | A panel in the darkest background of the theme (`UIColors.BackgroundDark`, the page behind the other surfaces). Fills its parent; follows a change of the theme. |
| `CreateElevated()` | A panel one step lighter than the medium one (`UIColors.BackgroundMediumElevated`, raised against a medium surface). Fills its parent; follows a change of the theme. |
| `CreateMedium()` | A panel in the medium background of the theme (`UIColors.BackgroundMedium`, the usual surface of a window). Fills its parent; follows a change of the theme. |
| `CreatePrimary()` | A panel in a very dark shade of the accent (`UIColors.PrimaryDarkDark`). Fills its parent; follows a change of the theme and of the accent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | The usual panel: the medium background of the theme, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreateMedium`. With a color set the panel is in the basic color of the set (a panel has no states that a set could color further); set `BackColor` for another color, it stays when the theme changes. `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary` is not the accent set but a very dark shade of the accent. |
| `CreateTransparent()` | A panel without a background of its own: what lies behind it shows through. Does not dock (`DockStyle.None`). |

### UIStyles.ProgressBars

Progress bars in the colors of the theme (continuous by default, not blocky like the standard control; Blocks and Marquee can be set). Cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.ProgressBar` for what the standard control does not have: `BorderStyle` (the thin border around the bar, on by default), a `BackColor` of `Transparent` (the track then takes the color of the panel the bar lies on, also when it changes, and in both themes; independent of the border), `Text` and `ShowPercentage` written on the bar (`TextAlign` and `PercentageAlign` place them), `TextScroll` for a text that is too long, `ShowFullTextToolTip`, and the colors of the border and of the text (`BorderColor`, `TextColor`, `TextOnFillColor`; the fill and the track are `ForeColor` and `BackColor`).

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateGreen()` | The same as `CreateStandard(UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Green)`: a fixed green fill. |
| `CreatePrimary()` | The same as `CreateStandard(UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Primary)`: the fill follows the app-wide accent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | Neutral gray fill by default, or the color of a color set; set `ForeColor` for any other color. |
| `CreateStatus()` | Fill color follows Value instead of being fixed - red at Minimum, yellow at the midpoint, green at Maximum, blending smoothly between them. For a "status/health" bar where color communicates good/bad. |

### UIStyles.PropertyTables

A key/value `PropertyTable` (label + editor per row, grouped into sections) - typical use is a settings/options panel.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | Same, but the lines at the section headers have the theme accent (and follow a change of it). |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | A neutral table, or one with a line in the color of a color set at the left edge of every section header. |

### UIStyles.RadioButtons

Themed `RadioButton`s, drawn by the library: `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreateStandard` (neutral gray when selected) and `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreatePrimary` (the accent color), each also as a label-less `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreateStandardCompact` / `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreatePrimaryCompact`. A color set can be given to any of the standard ones. Hover, pressed, keyboard focus and disabled are built in. Radio buttons with the same parent form one group: put each group in its own panel.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "", bool isChecked = false)` | Like `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreateStandard` but with the button filled in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.CheckBoxes.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreatePrimaryCompact(bool isChecked = false)` | Like `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreateStandardCompact` but in the current accent - the compact counterpart to `UIStyles.RadioButtons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", bool isChecked = false, UIColorSet colors = null)` |  |
| `CreateStandardCompact(bool isChecked = false, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A button without a label, 25 x 25 (for table cells and the like). |

### UIStyles.SlimProgressBars

A thin, fully custom-drawn `SlimProgressBar` for slim status-strip-style indicators rather than a prominent, full-size bar (see `UIStyles.ProgressBars`). It is a plain control, with a `Text`, `ShowPercentage` and `TextPosition` for a message next to the strip, and `TextScroll` for a text that is too long.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateGreen()` | The same as `CreateStandard(UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Green)`: a fixed green fill. |
| `CreatePrimary()` | The same as `CreateStandard(UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Primary)`: the fill follows the app-wide accent. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | Neutral gray fill by default, or the color of a color set; set `ForeColor` for any other color. |
| `CreateStatus()` | Fill color follows Value instead of being fixed - red at Minimum, yellow at the midpoint, green at Maximum, blending smoothly between them. For a "status/health" bar where color communicates good/bad. |

### UIStyles.Spinners

A rotating `Spinner` for "loading ..." states. Plain variants are neutral gray, the color of a color set, fixed green or the theme accent; `CreateStatus` blends the arc red → yellow → green by `Value`; the `CreateProgress*` versions also write that value as a percentage in the centre (raise it as the load advances). A text next to the ring, the speed, a known load and the rest are properties of the `Spinner`.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateGreen(int size = 24, int thickness = 0)` | The same as `CreateStandard(size, thickness, UIStyles.Colors.Sets.Green)`: a fixed green spinner. |
| `CreatePrimary(int size = 24, int thickness = 0)` | The arc follows the theme accent. |
| `CreateProgressGreen(int size = 40, int thickness = 0)` | A green spinner that also shows a percentage in the centre (starts at 0). |
| `CreateProgressPrimary(int size = 40, int thickness = 0)` | An accent spinner that also shows a percentage in the centre (starts at 0). |
| `CreateProgressStandard(int size = 40, int thickness = 0, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A gray spinner (or one in the color of a color set) that also shows a percentage in the centre (starts at 0; 40 px by default - a ring smaller than about 30 px leaves the digits out as not legible). |
| `CreateProgressStatus(int size = 40, int thickness = 0)` | Shows a percentage in the centre; the arc is a solid color blended red (0) → yellow → green (100) by that value. |
| `CreateStandard(int size = 24, int thickness = 0, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A neutral-gray spinner, or one in the color of a color set; set `ArcColor` for any other color. |
| `CreateStatus(int size = 24, int thickness = 0)` | The arc is a solid color blended red (0) → yellow → green (100) by `Value` (starts at 0 - raise it as the load advances); no number in the centre. |

### UIStyles.Symbols

Ready-made symbols as text characters - plus, trash can, arrows, gear, lock and so on - for buttons, labels and menu items. Being text, they take the color of the control they are on and scale with its font.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `GetFontName(string symbol)` | The name of the font a symbol has to be drawn in. Most are drawn in `UIStyles.Fonts.Icon`; the ones that come from the Windows icon font (`Delete`, `Print`, `Filter`, `Lightning` ... - every symbol whose character is in the private-use range) need "Segoe MDL2 Assets", which Windows 10 and 11 have; `Copy` uses "Segoe Fluent Icons" where Windows has it (Windows 11). Without the icon font the usual font is returned, so nothing throws - but those symbols then show as boxes. `UIStyles.Buttons.CreateSymbol` picks the right one by itself; use this when you draw a symbol yourself. |

### UIStyles.TabControls

A themed `TabControl` - behaves like the standard one, drawn in the library's own look.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | Like `UIStyles.TabControls.CreateStandard` but with the selected tab's bar and the menu selection in the current accent instead of neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.DataGridViews.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateReadOnlyPrimary()` | Like `UIStyles.TabControls.CreateReadOnlyStandard` but with the selected tab's bar in the current accent - the read-only counterpart to `UIStyles.TabControls.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateReadOnlyStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | The display-only variant - tabs can be switched, not added, renamed or closed. Use `UIStyles.TabControls.CreateStandard` instead for editable tabs. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | The editable variant - right-click a tab to add, rename or close tabs. Use `UIStyles.TabControls.CreateReadOnlyStandard` instead for tabs the user cannot edit. |

### UIStyles.TableLayoutPanels

Themed `TableLayoutPanel`s, pre-sized to the given column/row count. Otherwise the standard control (`ColumnStyles`, `RowStyles`, `GrowStyle`, `AutoScroll` with scroll bars in the style of the theme ...). There is no frame and there are no lines between the cells by default. Set `BorderStyle = FixedSingle` for a thin frame in the color of the theme; cast the result to `ErikwnkWFUI.Controls.TableLayoutPanel` for `BorderColor`, and for the lines of `CellBorderStyle = Single`: `CellBorderColor` (also `InnerCellBorderColor` and `OuterCellBorderColor` for the lines between the cells and the ones around the table) and `CellBorderLines` (all lines, only the ones around the table or only the ones between the cells). The tables do not dock (`Dock` is left to the caller). Right-to-left layouts are not supported.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateDark(int columnCount, int rowCount)` | A table layout panel in the darkest background of the theme (`UIColors.BackgroundDark`, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreateDark`), without margin and padding. Follows a change of the theme. |
| `CreatePrimary(int columnCount, int rowCount)` | A table layout panel in a very dark shade of the accent (`UIColors.PrimaryDarkDark`, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary`), without margin and padding. Follows a change of the theme and of the accent. |
| `CreateStandard(int columnCount, int rowCount, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A table layout panel in the elevated background of the theme (`UIColors.BackgroundMediumElevated`, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreateElevated`), without margin and padding. Follows a change of the theme. |
| `CreateTransparent(int columnCount, int rowCount)` | A table layout panel without a background of its own (what lies behind it shows through), otherwise like `UIStyles.TableLayoutPanels.CreateStandard`. |

### UIStyles.TextBoxes

Themed `TextBox`es.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateBorderless(string text = "", string placeholder = "")` | A text box without a frame (the fill and the text follow the theme as on `UIStyles.TextBoxes.CreateStandard`). |
| `CreateBorderstyleNone(string text = "", string placeholder = "")` | The old name of `UIStyles.TextBoxes.CreateBorderless`; it is removed once the projects that use it have been changed. |
| `CreateLockable(string text = "", string placeholder = "", bool locked = true, UIColorSet colors = null)` | A text box that is locked (read-only) until the user unlocks it with the pencil in the box: the pencil starts the editing (the box is unlocked, has the focus and has its text selected), the check mark or the Enter key accepts the text and locks it again, the Escape key gives the old text back; F2 or Enter on the locked box start the editing too. `IsLocked`, `LockedChanged`, `EditAccepted` and `EditCancelled` tell the application what happens. |
| `CreatePassword(string text = "", string placeholder = "", UIColorSet colors = null)` | A text box for a password: what is typed is hidden, and an eye in the box (or the keys Alt+F8) shows it with a click and hides it again with the next one (the tooltip with the whole text of a box that is too narrow only appears while the password is shown). |
| `CreatePrimary(string text = "", string placeholder = "")` | Same, but the frame has the theme accent while the box has the focus (the other parameters as there). |
| `CreateStandard(string text = "", string placeholder = "", UIColorSet colors = null)` | A text box with a quiet frame that has the text color while the box has the focus, or the color of a color set. |

### UIStyles.TitledListBoxes

A `ListBox` with a title above it - see `UIStyles.ListBoxes` for the list box on its own. Everything else is the same as the list box.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(string headerTitle = null, string displayMember = null, bool allowReorder = false, bool showEnumeration = false, ContentAlignment headerTextAlign = MiddleLeft)` | Like `UIStyles.TitledListBoxes.CreateStandard` but with the selection and the drop line in the current accent instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.ListBoxes.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(string headerTitle = null, string displayMember = null, bool allowReorder = false, bool showEnumeration = false, ContentAlignment headerTextAlign = MiddleLeft, UIColorSet colors = null)` | The titled list box in neutral gray. |

### UIStyles.Toasts

A small message that closes itself, shown in a window (below the middle by default). It belongs to that window (moves with it, never takes the focus) and is shown only while the window is in front; a toast that cannot be shown waits for it. See `ToastForm`.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Like `UIStyles.Toasts.CreateStandard` but in the current accent color - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Creates the settings of a toast as properties, to show toasts with them again and again (`Show`); in the neutral gray unless `colors` says otherwise. |
| `ShowPrimary(string message, Form owner, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Like `UIStyles.Toasts.ShowStandard` but in the current accent color instead of the neutral gray - mirrors `UIStyles.Buttons.CreatePrimary`. |
| `ShowPrimary(InfoPopupSection content, Form owner, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Like `UIStyles.Toasts.ShowPrimary`, with a title and, if wanted, own colors for the title and the message. |
| `ShowStandard(string message, Form owner, UIColorSet colors = null, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Shows a toast in the neutral gray. |
| `ShowStandard(InfoPopupSection content, Form owner, UIColorSet colors = null, PopupTransparency transparency = Medium, PopupDuration duration = Medium, PopupDelay delay = Instant, ToastIcon icon = None, string symbol = null, ToastPosition position = BelowCenter)` | Shows a toast in the neutral gray with a title above the message and, if wanted, own colors for each (see `InfoPopupSection`). |

### UIStyles.ToggleSwitches

iOS-style on/off `ToggleSwitch`es: `CreateStandard` is gray while it is on, `CreatePrimary` follows the accent, and `colors:` takes the colors of a set.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(bool isChecked = true, string tooltipChecked = null, string tooltipUnchecked = null, Size? size = null)` | Same, but the switch follows the theme accent while it is on (the other parameters as there). |
| `CreateStandard(bool isChecked = true, string tooltipChecked = null, string tooltipUnchecked = null, UIColorSet colors = null, Size? size = null)` | A switch that is gray while it is on, or in the colors of a color set. |

### UIStyles.ToolTips

Creates a plain `ToolTip` component - note it isn't owned by any control, so dispose it yourself if you're not letting it live for the app's whole lifetime.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateToolTip(string text = "")` | A tooltip in the colors of the theme (they follow a change of it; a color set by hand stays). |

### UIStyles.TrackBars

A slim, theme-matching horizontal `TrackBar`; with the value popup and a percent format it is a volume slider.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(double value = 0, double maximum = 1, bool showValuePopup = false, Func<double, string> formatValue = null, UIColorSet popupColors = null)` | Same, but the fill and thumb follow the theme accent (`value`, `maximum`, `showValuePopup`, `formatValue` and `popupColors` as there). |
| `CreateStandard(double value = 0, double maximum = 1, UIColorSet colors = null, bool showValuePopup = false, Func<double, string> formatValue = null, UIColorSet popupColors = null)` | A neutral-gray slider, or one in the color of a color set; any other color: pass it as `colors` (a color set, or simply a color). |

### UIStyles.VersionPanels

A narrow strip with the version of the program (the entry assembly, like "v1.2.3"; `VersionText` changes it) at its right end and, while an update is known, a small green button next to it. It is the version strip of a settings window as an element of its own, for any window or page: put it in, and announce an update with `ShowUpdate(appUpdater, result)` or let `await CheckForUpdateAsync(appUpdater, timeout)` look for one. A click on the button shows the update prompt of the `AppUpdater` over the window the strip is in. Docks at the bottom (`Dock` can be changed); follows a change of the theme and of the accent.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary()` | The strip in a very dark shade of the accent, the same as `UIStyles.Panels.CreatePrimary`. |
| `CreateStandard(UIColorSet colors = null)` | The strip in the darkest background of the theme (the same as the version strip of a settings window), or with a color set in its basic color. |

### UIStyles.VolumeControls

A `VolumeControl` for audio: a mute button (a loudspeaker, crossed out while it is muted) with a slider beside it, as on video sites. The volume is remembered while it is muted, the key M on the slider mutes too, and the slider shows the percentage in a popup. Read `EffectiveVolume` for what the audio output is to get, and react to `VolumeChanged`.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreatePrimary(double volume = 1, Size? size = null, bool showPercentage = false, IAudioVolume target = null)` | Same, but the slider and its popup follow the theme accent (`volume`, `size`, `showPercentage` and `target` as there). |
| `CreateStandard(double volume = 1, UIColorSet colors = null, Size? size = null, bool showPercentage = false, IAudioVolume target = null)` | A volume control with a gray slider, or one in the color of a color set. |
